sentences.zh: 李乂，本名尚真，趙州房子人也。

translations.literal: Li Yi—Li Yi, original personal name Shangzhen, was a native of Fangzi in Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, whose original name was Shangzhen, came from Fangzi in Zhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少與兄尚一、尚貞俱以文章見稱，舉進士。

translations.literal: In youth he and his elder brothers Shangyi and Shangzhen were all famed for literary talent and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he and his brothers Shangyi and Shangzhen were all celebrated for their writing and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period he rose through successive appointments to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 時中宗遣使江南分道贖生，以所在官物充直。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhongzong sent envoys to Jiangnan by separate routes to ransom living creatures for release, using official goods from each locality as payment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Zhongzong dispatched envoys to the Jiangnan region by separate routes to buy captive animals for release, paying with official goods held in each district.

sentences.zh: 乂上疏曰：「江南水鄉，采捕為業，魚鱉之利，黎元所資，土地使然，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial saying: "The Jiangnan region is a land of rivers and lakes; hunting and fishing are its livelihood. The profit of fish and turtles is what the common people rely on for support. The land makes this so, and it has been so from of old.
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial that read: "Jiangnan is a country of waterways; gathering and fishing are its trades. Fish and turtles are what the people live on—the land has made it so since long ago.

sentences.zh: 伏以聖慈含育，恩周動植，布天下之大德，及鱗介之微品。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your sagely compassion nourishes and bears all things, extending grace to both moving and rooted life, spreading the great virtue of the empire even to the smallest scaly and shelled creatures.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that Your Majesty's sacred kindness nurtures all life, extending favor to every plant and animal, spreading imperial virtue even to the tiniest fish and shellfish.

sentences.zh: 雖雲雨之私，有霑於末類；

translations.literal: Though the private favor of cloud and rain may reach the lowliest kinds;
translations.idiomatic: Though the gentle rain of grace may touch even the humblest creatures;

sentences.zh: 而生成之惠，未洽於平人。

translations.literal: the bounty of sustaining life has not yet fully reached ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: the blessing of nurturing life has not yet fully reached the common people.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 江湖之饒，生育無限；

translations.literal: The abundance of rivers and lakes breeds without limit;
translations.idiomatic: Rivers and lakes teem with life beyond measure;

sentences.zh: 府庫之用，支供易殫。

translations.literal: the expenditures of the treasury are easily exhausted in supplying them.
translations.idiomatic: yet treasury outlays to support the policy are quickly spent dry.

sentences.zh: 費之若少，則所濟何成；

translations.literal: if the expense is small, then what is accomplished by the relief?
translations.idiomatic: If the expense is modest, little is actually saved;

sentences.zh: 用之倘多，則常支有闕。

translations.literal: if the use is large, then the regular outlays will fall short.
translations.idiomatic: if it is large, the ordinary budget will fall short.

sentences.zh: 在於拯物，豈若憂人。

translations.literal: When it comes to saving creatures, how does that compare to caring for people?
translations.idiomatic: To rescue animals—how can that compare with relieving human distress?

sentences.zh: 且鬻生之徒，唯利斯視，錢刀日至，網罟年滋，施之一朝，營之百倍，未若回救贖之錢物，減困貧之徭賦，活國愛人，其福勝彼。」

translations.literal: Moreover, those who sell living things look only to profit; coins arrive daily and nets increase year by year. A single day's expenditure yields a hundredfold return. Better to turn back the funds used for ransoming and reduce corvée and taxes burdening the poor and distressed—saving the state and loving the people brings greater blessing than that."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, sellers of captive animals care only for profit: money flows in every day and nets multiply year by year. One day's outlay from the court yields a hundredfold in their trade. Far better to divert the ransom funds and lighten levies on the poor—reviving the state and cherishing the people would bring a greater blessing still."

sentences.zh: 乂知制誥凡數載。

translations.literal: Yi drafted imperial edicts for several years in all.
translations.idiomatic: For several years Yi served as drafter of imperial proclamations.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，遷吏部侍郎，與宋璟、盧從願同時典選，銓敘平允，甚為當時所稱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; together with Song Jing and Lu Congyuan he concurrently managed selection, conducting appointments with fairness, and was greatly praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 1 he became Vice Minister of Personnel. He shared charge of appointments with Song Jing and Lu Congyuan, and their even-handed evaluations won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 尋轉黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗令造金仙、玉真二觀，乂頻上疏諫，帝每優容之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ruizong ordered construction of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected monasteries; Yi repeatedly submitted memorials in remonstrance, and the emperor each time treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ordered the building of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected monasteries, Yi memorialized repeatedly in protest, and the emperor each time received him leniently.

sentences.zh: 開元初，特令乂與中書侍郎蘇颋纂集起居註，錄其嘉謨昌言可體國經遠者，別編奏之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was specially ordered, together with Vice Minister of the Secretariat Su Ting, to compile the Diaries of Activity and Repose, selecting excellent plans and splendid words fit to embody statecraft and guide the distant future, editing them separately and submitting them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he was specially assigned, with Secretariat Vice Minister Su Ting, to compile the court diaries, extract counsel and speeches that could serve long-range statecraft, and present them in a separate memorial.

sentences.zh: 乂在門下，多所駁正。

translations.literal: While Yi served in the Chancellery, he often rejected and corrected documents.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Chancellery, Yi frequently struck down or revised draft documents.

sentences.zh: 開元初，姚崇為紫微令，薦乂為紫微侍郎，外托薦賢，其實引在己下，去其糾駁之權也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan Yao Chong was Director of the Purple Tenuity Bureau; he recommended Yi as Vice Director, outwardly on the pretext of promoting the worthy, but in fact drawing him beneath himself and removing his power to criticize and correct.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, when Yao Chong headed the Purple Tenuity Bureau, he recommended Yi as vice director—ostensibly to advance talent, but in truth to place him under his own authority and strip him of the power to review and reject.

sentences.zh: 俄拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 乂方雅有學識，朝廷稱其有宰相之望，會病卒。

translations.literal: Yi was refined and possessed learning; the court said he had the makings of a chief minister, but he happened to die of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Refined and learned, Yi was spoken of at court as a man with the makings of a chief minister, but he died of illness before that could come to pass.

sentences.zh: 兄尚一，清源尉，早卒；

translations.literal: His elder brother Shangyi, magistrate of Qingyuan, died early;
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shangyi, magistrate of Qingyuan, died young;

sentences.zh: 尚貞，官至博州刺史。

translations.literal: Shangzhen rose to governor of Bo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhen rose to serve as governor of Bo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同為一集，號曰《李氏花萼集》，總二十卷。

translations.literal: The brothers jointly compiled one collection, entitled Collected Writings of the Li Brothers at the Flower Calyx Pavilion, twenty juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers jointly published a collection called the Li Brothers' Flower Calyx Anthology, twenty juan in all.

sentences.zh: 薛登，本名謙光，常州義興人也。

translations.literal: Xue Deng—Xue Deng, original personal name Qian'guang, was a native of Yixing in Chang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Deng, whose original name was Qian'guang, came from Yixing in Chang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父士通，大業中為鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: His father Shitong served as General of Soaring Hawks during the Daye reign.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shitong was a General of Soaring Hawks in the Daye era.

sentences.zh: 江都之亂，士通與鄉人聞人嗣安等同據本郡，以禦寇賊。

translations.literal: During the turmoil at Jiangdu, Shitong together with his fellow townsman Wenren Sian and others jointly held their home commandery to repel bandits and rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos engulfed Jiangdu, Shitong joined his countryman Wenren Sian and others in holding their home commandery against marauders.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，遣使歸國，高祖嘉之，降璽書勞勉，拜東武州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude he sent envoys to submit to the dynasty; Emperor Gaozu commended him, issued an imperial letter of commendation and encouragement, and appointed him governor of Dongwu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2 he sent envoys to pledge allegiance. Emperor Gaozu praised him, sent an imperial letter of encouragement, and appointed him governor of Dongwu.

sentences.zh: 俄而輔公祏於江都構逆，遣其將西門君儀等寇常州，士通率兵拒戰，大破之，君儀等僅以身免。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Fu Gongshi rebelled at Jiangdu and sent his generals Ximen Junyi and others to raid Chang prefecture; Shitong led troops to resist, inflicted a great defeat, and Junyi and the others barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fu Gongshi rose in rebellion at Jiangdu and sent generals such as Ximen Junyi against Chang. Shitong met them in battle, routed them utterly, and Junyi's party escaped only with their lives.

sentences.zh: 及公祏平，累功封臨汾侯。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was pacified, Shitong's accumulated merit earned him enfeoffment as Marquis of Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: After Gongshi's defeat, his accumulated merit won him the title Marquis of Linfen.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷遷泉州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was promoted in succession to governor of Quan prefecture and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he rose to governor of Quan prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 謙光博涉文史，每與人談論前代故事，必廣引證驗，有如目擊。

translations.literal: Qian'guang was broadly versed in literature and history; whenever he discussed stories of former ages with others, he invariably cited wide proofs and verification, as though he had seen them himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qian'guang was widely read in letters and history. When he discussed events of earlier times, he cited evidence so fully that he seemed to have witnessed them himself.

sentences.zh: 少與徐堅、劉子玄齊名友善。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed on equal terms with Xu Jian and Liu Zixuan and was on friendly terms with them.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he ranked with Xu Jian and Liu Zixuan in reputation and counted them among his close friends.

sentences.zh: 文明中，解褐閬中主簿。

translations.literal: During the Wenming era he left the commoner's garb and was appointed chief clerk of Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: During Wenming he entered official service as chief clerk of Langzhong.

sentences.zh: 天授中，為左補闕，時選舉頗濫，謙光上疏曰：臣聞國以得賢為寶，臣以舉士為忠。

translations.literal: During the Tianshou era he served as Left Remonstrator; at that time appointments were quite lax, and Qian'guang submitted a memorial saying: Your servant has heard that a state treasures the acquisition of worthy men, and a minister's loyalty lies in recommending scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou period he became Left Remonstrator. Appointments had grown lax, and Qian'guang submitted a memorial that began: "A state is enriched by worthy men, and a minister proves loyalty by recommending talent."

sentences.zh: 是以子皮之讓國僑，鮑叔之推管仲，燕昭委兵於樂毅，苻堅托政於王猛。

translations.literal: Therefore Zipi yielded to Zichan, Bao Shuqi recommended Guan Zhong, King Zhao of Yan entrusted troops to Yue Yi, and Fu Jian delegated governance to Wang Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Zipi yielded office to Zichan; Bao Shuqi pushed Guan Zhong forward; King Zhao of Yan placed his armies in Yue Yi's hands; and Fu Jian entrusted the government to Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 子產受國人之謗，夷吾貪共賈之財，昭王錫輅馬以止讒，永固戮樊世以除譖。

translations.literal: Zichan endured slander from his countrymen; Guan Zhong was greedy for shared merchant wealth; King Zhao bestowed chariots and horses to stop calumny; and Fu Jian executed Fan Shi to remove slander.
translations.idiomatic: Zichan bore the people's reproach; Guan Zhong coveted merchants' shared profits; King Zhao rewarded chariots and horses to silence slander; and Fu Jian put Fan Shi to death to remove false accusation.

sentences.zh: 處猜嫌而益信，行間毀而無疑，此由默而識之，委而察之深也。

translations.literal: Amid suspicion they grew more trusted; amid slander they remained unquestioned—this came from silent recognition and deep observation through delegation.
translations.idiomatic: Under suspicion they won greater trust; under slander they stayed above doubt—because rulers recognized them quietly and watched them closely through delegated authority.

sentences.zh: 至若宰我見愚於宣尼，逢萌被知於文叔，韓信無聞於項氏，毛遂不齒於平原，此失士之故也。

translations.literal: As for Zai Wo being seen as foolish by Confucius, Feng Meng being recognized by Emperor Guangwu, Han Xin going unheard under Xiang Yu, and Mao Sui held in low esteem by Lord Pingyuan—these were cases of losing worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Wo was judged foolish by Confucius; Feng Meng was discovered by Emperor Guangwu; Han Xin went unnoticed under Xiang Yu; Mao Sui was slighted by Lord Pingyuan—all failures to keep talent.

sentences.zh: 是以人主受不肖之士則政乖，得賢良之佐則時泰，故堯資八元而庶績其理，周任十亂而天下和平。

translations.literal: Therefore when a ruler accepts unworthy men governance goes awry; when he obtains worthy and virtuous assistants the age is peaceful. Thus Yao relied on the Eight Worthies and all achievements were well ordered; King Wen of Zhou employed the Ten Wise Ministers and the realm was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler takes unworthy men, government goes wrong; when he gains worthy assistants, the age grows calm. Yao relied on the Eight Worthies and good order followed; King Wen of Zhou used the Ten Wise Ministers and the realm was at peace.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，則士不可不察，而官不可妄授也。

translations.literal: From this it follows that scholars cannot be left unexamined and offices cannot be recklessly bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that talent must be scrutinized and office must not be given rashly.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 比來舉薦，多不以才，假譽馳聲，互相推獎，希潤身之小計，忘臣子之大猷，非所以報國求賢，副陛下翹翹之望者也。

translations.literal: Recent recommendations have mostly not been based on talent. False reputations and spreading fame are used to push and praise one another, coveting petty schemes for personal gain while forgetting the great duty of minister and subject. This is not the way to repay the state, seek the worthy, or fulfill Your Majesty's lofty expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Lately recommendations have seldom rested on real ability. Men trade inflated praise, promote one another's fame, and chase small personal gains while forgetting a subject's larger duty. That is no way to serve the state, find talent, or meet Your Majesty's high hopes.

sentences.zh: 臣竊窺古之取士，實異於今。

translations.literal: Your servant privately observes that the ancient method of selecting scholars was truly different from today's.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that the ancients chose officials very differently from us.

sentences.zh: 先觀名行之源，考其鄉邑之譽，崇禮讓以勵己，明節義以標信，以敦樸為先最，以雕蟲為後科。

translations.literal: First they observed the source of reputation and conduct, examined local repute, honored ritual and deference to encourage self-cultivation, clarified integrity and righteousness to mark trustworthiness, prioritized sincerity and plainness as foremost, and relegated literary embellishment to a secondary consideration.
translations.idiomatic: They first looked to the roots of a man's name and conduct, weighed local reputation, honored courtesy and humility, made integrity the mark of trust, put plain sincerity first and literary ornament last.

sentences.zh: 故人崇勸讓之風，士去輕浮之行。

translations.literal: Therefore people upheld the custom of encouragement and deference, and scholars abandoned frivolous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: People then valued mutual encouragement and deference, and scholars shed frivolous ways.

sentences.zh: 希仕者必修貞確不拔之操，行難進易退之規。

translations.literal: Those seeking office necessarily cultivated unshakeable integrity and followed the principle of being hard to advance and easy to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Men who sought office had to cultivate steadfast integrity and the rule of entering office with difficulty and leaving it with ease.

sentences.zh: 眾議以定其高下，郡將難誣於曲直。

translations.literal: Public deliberation determined their standing high or low, and the commandery commander could hardly distort right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion fixed their rank, and prefectural commanders could scarcely twist right into wrong.

sentences.zh: 故計貢之賢愚，即州將之榮辱；

translations.literal: Thus the worthiness or folly of the recommended tribute reflected the honor or disgrace of the commandery governor;
translations.idiomatic: A district's tribute candidates reflected honor or shame on its governor;

sentences.zh: 穢行之彰露，亦鄉人之厚顏。

translations.literal: the exposure of vile conduct also brought shame to fellow villagers.
translations.idiomatic: and exposed misconduct shamed the whole community.

sentences.zh: 是以李陵降而隴西慚，幹木隱而西河美。

translations.literal: Therefore when Li Ling surrendered Longxi felt ashamed; when Duan Ganmu lived in seclusion Xihe was praised.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ling surrendered, Longxi was ashamed; when Duan Ganmu withdrew from office, Xihe was praised.

sentences.zh: 故名勝於利，則小人之道消；

translations.literal: Hence when reputation prevails over profit the way of petty men declines;
translations.idiomatic: When reputation outweighs profit, petty conduct fades;

sentences.zh: 利勝於名，則貪暴之風扇。

translations.literal: when profit prevails over reputation the wind of greed and violence fans.
translations.idiomatic: when profit outweighs reputation, greed and violence spread.

sentences.zh: 是以化俗之本，須擯輕浮。

translations.literal: Therefore the foundation of transforming custom lies in rejecting the frivolous.
translations.idiomatic: The root of changing custom, then, is to drive out frivolity.

sentences.zh: 昔冀缺以禮讓升朝，則晉人知禮；

translations.literal: In the past when Ji Que was promoted to court through ritual deference the people of Jin understood ritual;
translations.idiomatic: When Ji Que entered court through courtesy and deference, the people of Jin learned ritual;

sentences.zh: 文翁以儒林獎俗，則蜀士多儒。

translations.literal: when Wen Weng encouraged custom through Confucian learning many scholars in Shu became Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: when Wen Weng used Confucian schools to reform custom, Shu produced many scholars.

sentences.zh: 燕昭好馬，則駿馬來庭；

translations.literal: King Zhao of Yan loved horses, and fine steeds came to his court;
translations.idiomatic: King Zhao of Yan loved horses, and fine steeds came to court;

sentences.zh: 葉公好龍，則真龍入室。

translations.literal: Lord Ye loved dragons, and a true dragon entered his chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Ye loved dragons, and a real dragon entered his hall.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，未有上之所好而下不從其化者也。

translations.literal: From this it is said that there has never been a case where those above had a preference and those below did not follow their transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Never yet has a ruler's taste failed to reshape the conduct of those below.

sentences.zh: 自七國之季，雖雜縱橫，而漢代求才，猶征百行。

translations.literal: Since the end of the Warring States period, although mixed with the Vertical and Horizontal alliances, the Han dynasty's search for talent still sought all aspects of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the Warring States age, with its shifting alliances, Han still looked for men of full character.

sentences.zh: 是以禮節之士，敏德自修，閭裏推高，然後為府寺所辟。

translations.literal: Therefore scholars of ritual and integrity cultivated virtue themselves, were praised highly in their villages, and only then were recruited by government offices.
translations.idiomatic: Men of ritual and integrity refined themselves, won village esteem, and only then were summoned to office.

sentences.zh: 魏氏取人，尤愛放達；

translations.literal: The Wei dynasty selected men, particularly favoring unfettered freedom;
translations.idiomatic: Wei especially favored free and unrestrained men;

sentences.zh: 晉、宋之後，祗重門資。

translations.literal: after the Jin and Song dynasties they valued only family background.
translations.idiomatic: while Jin and Song came to value pedigree alone.

sentences.zh: 獎為人求官之風，乖授職惟賢之義。

translations.literal: This encouraged the custom of seeking office for others, contrary to the principle of bestowing office based solely on worthiness.
translations.idiomatic: That bred the habit of seeking posts through patrons and betrayed the rule that office should follow merit.

sentences.zh: 有梁薦士，雅愛屬詞；

translations.literal: The Liang dynasty recommended scholars, especially loving literary composition;
translations.idiomatic: Liang favored literary composition in its recommendations;

sentences.zh: 陳氏簡賢，特珍賦詠。

translations.literal: the Chen dynasty selected the worthy, particularly treasuring poetic rhapsodies.
translations.idiomatic: Chen prized rhapsody and verse above all else.

sentences.zh: 故其俗以詩酒為重，不以修身為務。

translations.literal: Consequently their custom valued poetry and wine and did not make self-cultivation the duty.
translations.idiomatic: Their age therefore exalted poetry and wine and neglected self-cultivation.

sentences.zh: 逮至隋室，餘風尚在，開皇中李諤論之於文帝曰：「魏之三祖，更好文詞，忽君人之大道，好雕蟲之小藝。

translations.literal: By the Sui dynasty the remnants of this custom still remained. During the Kaihuang era Li E discussed this with Emperor Wen, saying: "The Three Ancestors of Wei were even more fond of literary phrases, neglecting the great way of ruling the people and favoring the petty skill of literary embellishment.
translations.idiomatic: Sui still retained that habit. In Kaihuang, Li E told Emperor Wen: "Wei's Three Ancestors loved polished phrasing, ignored the ruler's great task, and prized petty literary craft.

sentences.zh: 連篇累牘，不出月露之形；

translations.literal: Piles of documents page after page contained nothing beyond the shapes of moon and dew;
translations.idiomatic: Documents piled up page after page with nothing but moonlight and dew;

sentences.zh: 積案盈箱，唯是風雲之狀。

translations.literal: cases and boxes overflowed filled only with descriptions of wind and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: cases overflowed with wind and cloud alone.

sentences.zh: 代俗以此相高，朝廷以茲擢士，故文筆日煩，其政日亂」。

translations.literal: The common custom of the age esteemed this, and the court used this to select scholars; therefore literary style grew increasingly verbose and governance grew increasingly chaotic."
translations.idiomatic: The age took that for refinement, and the court promoted men by it—so writing grew ever more ornate and government ever more disorderly."

sentences.zh: 帝納李諤之策，由是下制禁斷文筆浮詞。

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted Li E's strategy, and thus issued an edict banning frivolous literary phrases.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Li E's proposal and issued an edict forbidding empty literary flourishes.

sentences.zh: 其年，泗洲刺史司馬幼之以表不典實得罪。

translations.literal: That year Sima Youzhi, prefect of Sizhou, was punished for submitting a memorial that was not classical and factual.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Sima Youzhi, prefect of Sizhou, was punished because his memorial was neither classical nor factual.

sentences.zh: 於是風俗改勵，政化大行。

translations.literal: Thereupon customs were reformed and encouraged, and governance was greatly improved.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were corrected, encouragement spread, and government improved sharply.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣興，又變前法，置進士等科。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang succeeded and revived, again changing the previous laws and establishing the Presented Scholar and other examinations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he changed the law again and established the Presented Scholar examination and related categories.

sentences.zh: 於是後生之徒，復相放效，因陋就寡，赴速邀時，緝綴小文，名之策學，不以指實為本，而以浮虛為貴。

translations.literal: Consequently the younger generation again imitated one another, clinging to the shallow and meager, rushing to meet the times, patching together minor compositions called policy studies, not taking factual substance as the basis but valuing emptiness and superficiality.
translations.idiomatic: Youth then imitated one another again: they clung to the shallow, chased deadlines, stitched together short essays called policy studies, and prized emptiness over substance.

sentences.zh: 有唐纂歷，雖漸革於故非；

translations.literal: The Tang dynasty inherited the mandate, gradually reforming past errors;
translations.idiomatic: Tang inherited the mandate and has slowly corrected old abuses;

sentences.zh: 陛下君臨，思察才於共理。

translations.literal: Your Majesty rules, considering how to examine talent for joint governance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now reigns and seeks to judge talent for shared rule.

sentences.zh: 樹本崇化，惟在旌賢。

translations.literal: Establishing the foundation and honoring transformation lies solely in honoring the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: To set the root and exalt reform, nothing matters more than honoring the worthy.

sentences.zh: 今之舉人，有乖事實。

translations.literal: Today's recommendation of men contradicts the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Today's recommendations no longer match reality.

sentences.zh: 鄉議決小人之筆，行修無長者之論。

translations.literal: Village deliberation is decided by the brush of petty men; conduct and cultivation lack the discourse of elders.
translations.idiomatic: Village opinion is settled by petty men's pens, and conduct reviews lack the judgment of elders.

sentences.zh: 策第喧競於州府，祈恩不勝於拜伏。

translations.literal: Competing noisily for examination ranking in the prefectures and commanderies, beseeching favor is surpassed only by prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates clamor for examination rank in prefectures and districts, and pleading for favor is outdone only by prostration.

sentences.zh: 或明制才出，試遣搜易攵，驅馳府寺之門，出入王公之第。

translations.literal: Sometimes as soon as the clear decree is issued they are sent to search and examine, galloping to the gates of government offices and entering and leaving the residences of princes and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes, as soon as the decree appears, they are sent to conduct searches, racing to government gates and in and out of princes' mansions.

sentences.zh: 上啟陳詩，唯希咳唾之澤；

translations.literal: Submitting petitions and presenting poems, hoping only for the favor of a cough or spit;
translations.idiomatic: They submit petitions and poems, hoping only for the droppings of patronage;

sentences.zh: 摩頂至足，冀荷提攜之恩。

translations.literal: from head to toe they hope to receive the grace of being lifted up.
translations.idiomatic: from head to foot they seek the favor of being raised up.

sentences.zh: 故俗號舉人，皆稱覓舉。

translations.literal: Therefore it is commonly said of those recommended that they are all called seekers of recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates are therefore commonly called seekers of recommendation.

sentences.zh: 覓為自求之稱，未是人知之辭。

translations.literal: Seeking is a term for self-seeking, not a phrase for being known by others.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking describes self-promotion, not being discovered by others.

sentences.zh: 察其行而度其材，則人品於茲見矣。

translations.literal: Observe their conduct and measure their talent, and their personal quality is thereby revealed.
translations.idiomatic: Watch their conduct and weigh their talent, and character shows itself at once.

sentences.zh: 徇己之心切，則至公之理乖；

translations.literal: When the heart bent on self-interest is intense the principle of utmost fairness is violated;
translations.idiomatic: When self-interest runs deep, fairness is lost;

sentences.zh: 貪仕之性彰，則廉潔之風薄。

translations.literal: when the nature greedy for office becomes evident the custom of integrity and honesty grows thin.
translations.idiomatic: when greed for office shows itself, integrity grows thin.

sentences.zh: 是知府命雖高，異叔度勤勤之讓；

translations.literal: Thus although the prefect's mandate is high it differs from the earnest deference of Huangfu Mi;
translations.idiomatic: A prefect's commission may be lofty, yet it is nothing like Huangfu Mi's earnest yielding;

sentences.zh: 黃門已貴，無秦嘉耿耿之辭。

translations.literal: although the Chamberlain's post is esteemed it lacks the sincere words of Qin Jia.
translations.idiomatic: the Yellow Gate may be honored, yet it lacks Qin Jia's steadfast refusal.

sentences.zh: 縱不能抑己推賢，亦不肯待於三命。

translations.literal: Even if they cannot restrain themselves and recommend the worthy, they are also unwilling to wait for the three summonses.
translations.idiomatic: Even when they cannot suppress self-interest and recommend others, they refuse to wait for the three summonses.

sentences.zh: 豈與夫白駒皎皎，不雜風塵，束帛戔戔，榮高物表，校量其廣狹也！

translations.literal: How can this compare to the gleaming white colt untainted by worldly dust, or the modest bundles of silk honored above material things—measuring their breadth and narrowness!
translations.idiomatic: How does that compare with the gleaming white colt unstained by dust, or humble silk honored above worldly things—measured by breadth of spirit!

sentences.zh: 是以耿介之士，羞自拔而致其辭；

translations.literal: Therefore upright and principled scholars are ashamed to promote themselves and offer their words;
translations.idiomatic: Principled men are ashamed to push themselves forward;

sentences.zh: 循常之人，舍其疏而取其附。

translations.literal: ordinary people abandon the distant and choose the attached.
translations.idiomatic: ordinary men discard the remote and choose the connected.

sentences.zh: 故選司補署，喧然於禮闈；

translations.literal: Thus the selection offices' appointments create a clamor within the ceremonial gates;
translations.idiomatic: Selection offices therefore buzz within the examination halls;

sentences.zh: 州貢賓王，爭訟於階闥。

translations.literal: the commandery tributes and guest scholars contend and dispute before the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: district tributes and guest scholars quarrel at the palace steps.

sentences.zh: 謗議紛合，浸以成風。

translations.literal: Slanderous discussions converge, gradually becoming a custom.
translations.idiomatic: Slander gathers and slowly becomes custom.

sentences.zh: 夫競榮者必有競利之心，謙遜者亦無貪賄之累。

translations.literal: Those who compete for glory necessarily have minds that compete for profit; the modest and deferential also bear no burden of coveting bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Those who chase glory chase profit as well; the modest bear no taint of bribery.

sentences.zh: 自非上智，焉能不移；

translations.literal: Unless one is of superior wisdom, how can one remain unmoved?
translations.idiomatic: Only the highest wisdom stays unmoved;

sentences.zh: 在於中人，理由習俗。

translations.literal: For the average person reason lies in custom.
translations.idiomatic: for ordinary men, habit decides all.

sentences.zh: 若重謹厚之士，則懷祿者必崇德以修名；

translations.literal: If we value cautious and sincere scholars, then those seeking emolument will necessarily honor virtue to cultivate reputation;
translations.idiomatic: If cautious and sincere men are honored, office-seekers will cultivate virtue to preserve their names;

sentences.zh: 若開趨競之門，邀仕者皆戚施而附會。

translations.literal: if we open the door to competition and currying favor, then those seeking office will all be sycophants and yes-men.
translations.idiomatic: if the door to rivalry is opened, every seeker becomes a flatterer and hanger-on.

sentences.zh: 附會則百姓罹其弊，潔己則兆庶蒙其福。

translations.literal: With sycophancy the common people suffer its harm; with self-purification the myriad masses receive its blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery harms the people; self-restraint blesses the masses.

sentences.zh: 故風化之漸，靡不由茲。

translations.literal: Therefore the gradual process of cultural transformation invariably stems from this.
translations.idiomatic: Every gradual change in custom begins here.

sentences.zh: 今訪鄉閭之談，唯祇歸於裏正。

translations.literal: Now if we inquire about village discussions they are solely entrusted to the village head.
translations.idiomatic: Village opinion today rests entirely with the village head.

sentences.zh: 縱使名虧禮則，罪掛刑章，或冒籍以偷資，或邀勛而竊級，假其不義之賂，則是無犯鄉閭。

translations.literal: Even if one's name violates ritual principles or one's crime falls under penal statutes, or one fraudulently registers to steal qualifications or seeks merit to steal rank—if one uses ill-gotten bribes then one has not offended the village.
translations.idiomatic: Even when a man breaks ritual, falls under the penal code, falsifies registration, or buys rank with stolen merit—if he pays improper bribes, the village is said to have no complaint.

sentences.zh: 豈得比郭有道之銓量，茅容望重，裴逸人之賞拔，夏少名高，語其優劣也！

translations.literal: How can this compare to Guo Youdao's evaluations where Mao Rong was held in high esteem, or Pei Yiren's recognition and promotion where Xia Shao was highly renowned—speaking of their superiority or inferiority!
translations.idiomatic: How can that compare with Guo Tai's weighing of men, Mao Rong's high standing, Pei Yiren's promotions, or Xia Shao's fame—judging true worth!

sentences.zh: 祇如才應經邦之流，唯令試策；

translations.literal: Merely, for those whose talent fits governing the state we only order them to sit for policy essays;
translations.idiomatic: For men fit to govern the state, we now require only policy essays;

sentences.zh: 武能制敵之例，只驗彎弧。

translations.literal: for examples of military ability to defeat the enemy we only test archery.
translations.idiomatic: for warriors able to defeat the enemy, we test only archery.

sentences.zh: 若其文擅清奇，便充甲第，藻思微減，便即告歸。

translations.literal: If their writing excels in clarity and originality they immediately fill the top grade; if their literary thought is slightly inferior they are immediately sent home.
translations.idiomatic: If writing is strikingly fine, they take first rank; if thought is slightly weaker, they are sent home at once.

sentences.zh: 以此收人，恐乖事實。

translations.literal: Selecting men in this way, I fear, contradicts the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing men this way, I fear, departs from reality.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 樂廣假筆於潘嶽，靈運詞高於穆之，平津文劣於長卿，子建筆麗於荀彧。

translations.literal: Yue Guang borrowed a brush from Pan Yue; Xie Lingyun's literary talent surpassed that of Xie Huilian; Gongsun Hong's writing was inferior to Sima Xiangru's; Cao Zhi's brush was more elegant than Xun Yu's.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Guang borrowed Pan Yue's pen; Xie Lingyun's prose outshone Xie Huilian's; Gongsun Hong wrote less well than Sima Xiangru; Cao Zhi's style surpassed Xun Yu's.

sentences.zh: 若以射策為最，則潘、謝、曹、馬必居孫、樂之右；

translations.literal: If ranking by examination essays were paramount, then Pan, Xie, Cao, and Sima would necessarily rank above Sun and Yue;
translations.idiomatic: If examination essays decided all, Pan, Xie, Cao, and Sima would rank above Sun and Yue;

sentences.zh: 若使協贊機猷，則安仁、靈運亦無裨附之益。

translations.literal: if they were to assist in planning strategies, then Pan Yue and Xie Lingyun would also be of no supplementary benefit.
translations.idiomatic: yet in planning strategy Pan Yue and Xie Lingyun would add little.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，不可一概而取也。

translations.literal: From this perspective they cannot be taken as a uniform standard.
translations.idiomatic: One standard, then, cannot fit every case.

sentences.zh: 至如武藝，則趙雲雖勇，資諸葛之指捴；

translations.literal: As for military skill, although Zhao Yun was brave he relied on Zhuge Liang's direction;
translations.idiomatic: In martial affairs Zhao Yun was brave but needed Zhuge Liang's direction;

sentences.zh: 周勃雖雄，乏陳平之計略。

translations.literal: although Zhou Bo was mighty he lacked Chen Ping's strategic planning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bo was formidable but lacked Chen Ping's strategy.

sentences.zh: 若使樊噲居蕭何之任，必失指縱之機；

translations.literal: If Fan Kuai were placed in Xiao He's position he would certainly miss the opportunity for direction and control;
translations.idiomatic: Place Fan Kuai in Xiao He's post and control would fail;

sentences.zh: 使蕭何入戲下之軍，亦無免主之效。

translations.literal: if Xiao He entered the army under command he would also lack the effectiveness of saving his lord.
translations.idiomatic: put Xiao He in the ranks under command and he could not save his lord.

sentences.zh: 鬥將長於摧鋒，謀將審於料事。

translations.literal: Combat generals excel in crushing the enemy's vanguard; strategic generals are careful in assessing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting generals excel at breaking the vanguard; planning generals excel at reading events.

sentences.zh: 是以文泉聚米，知隗囂之可圖；

translations.literal: Therefore by piling up rice Wen Quan knew that Wei Xiao could be plotted against;
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhong piled rice and saw that Wei Xiao could be taken;

sentences.zh: 陳湯屈指，識烏孫之自解。

translations.literal: by bending his fingers Chen Tang recognized that the Wusun would resolve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tang counted on his fingers and knew the Wusun would settle themselves.

sentences.zh: 八難之謀設，高祖追慚於酈生；

translations.literal: When the strategy of the eight difficulties was proposed Emperor Gaozu later felt ashamed before Li Yiji;
translations.idiomatic: When the eight difficulties were proposed, Emperor Gaozu later felt ashamed before Li Yiji;

sentences.zh: 九拒之計窮，公輸息心於伐宋。

translations.literal: when the plans of nine resistances were exhausted Gongshu Ban gave up his mind about attacking Song.
translations.idiomatic: when the nine defenses were exhausted, Gongshu Ban lost heart for attacking Song.

sentences.zh: 謀將不長於弓馬，良相寧資於射策。

translations.literal: Strategic generals do not excel in archery and horsemanship; good chief ministers—are they really aided by examination essays?
translations.idiomatic: Planning generals are not masters of bow and horse; great ministers are not chosen by examination essays.

sentences.zh: 豈與夫元長自表，妄飾詞鋒，曹植題章，虛飛麗藻，校量其可否也！

translations.literal: How can this compare to Yuan Chang's self-promotion falsely adorning his literary prowess, or Cao Zhi's inscribed chapters emptily flying with beautiful ornamentation—weighing their suitability or not!
translations.idiomatic: How does that compare with Yuan Chang's self-praise or Cao Zhi's ornate chapters—judging fitness by empty display!

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下降明制，頒峻科。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will issue a clear decree and promulgate rigorous criteria for selection.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask Your Majesty to issue clear rules and strict standards for selection.

sentences.zh: 千里一賢，尚不為少，僥幸冒進，須立堤防。

translations.literal: One worthy man per thousand li is still not too few; to prevent the opportunistic and reckless from advancing defenses must be established.
translations.idiomatic: One worthy man in a thousand li is not too many to hope for; opportunists who push forward must be blocked.

sentences.zh: 斷浮虛之飾詞，收實用之良策，不取無稽之說，必求忠告之言。

translations.literal: Cut off empty ornamental rhetoric and gather practical excellent strategies; do not accept unfounded theories but must seek loyal advice.
translations.idiomatic: Cut empty ornament, gather useful plans, reject groundless talk, and demand honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 文則試以效官，武則令其守禦，始既察言觀行，終亦循名責實，自然僥幸濫吹之伍，無所藏其妄庸。

translations.literal: For civil officials test them by entrusting them with office; for the military order them to defend and guard. First observe their words and scrutinize their conduct; ultimately hold them accountable for matching reputation with reality. Naturally the ranks of the opportunistic and incompetent will have nowhere to hide their folly.
translations.idiomatic: Test civil men by giving them office; test military men by assigning defense. First watch words and conduct; finally hold them to their names. Then the unworthy who slip through will have nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 故晏嬰云：「舉之以語，考之以事；

translations.literal: Therefore Yan Ying said: "Select them by their speech, examine them by their deeds;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying said: "Choose men by their words and test them by deeds;

sentences.zh: 寡其言而多其行，拙於文而工於事。」

translations.literal: value few words and many actions, clumsy in literary elegance but skilled in practical affairs."
translations.idiomatic: prefer few words and much action, plain writing and solid work."

sentences.zh: 此取人得賢之道也。

translations.literal: This is the way to obtain worthy men through selection.
translations.idiomatic: That is the way to choose worthy men.

sentences.zh: 其有武藝超絕，文鋒挺秀，有效伎之偏用，無經國之大才，為軍鋒之爪牙，作詞賦之標準。

translations.literal: As for those with exceptional martial prowess or outstanding literary talent, who have a particular skill for a specific function but lack the great talent for governing the state—those who serve as the claws and teeth of the army's vanguard or as the standard for poetry and rhapsody—
translations.idiomatic: Men of exceptional martial skill or literary brilliance may have special gifts yet lack talent to govern the state—claws and teeth for the army, or models for poetry and rhapsody—

sentences.zh: 自可試淩雲之策，練穿劄之工，承上命而賦《甘泉》，稟中軍而令赴敵，既有隨才之任，必無負乘之憂。

translations.literal: they may naturally be tested with strategies that soar to the clouds or trained in the skill of piercing armor. They may receive the imperial command to compose a Sweet Springs rhapsody or follow the central army's orders to face the enemy. Since there are appointments according to their talents there will certainly be no worry of failing in their duties.
translations.idiomatic: may be tested with soaring policy essays, trained in piercing armor, ordered to compose a Sweet Springs rhapsody, or sent under central command against the enemy. Appoint by talent, and none need fail in office.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案吳起臨戰，左右進劍，吳子曰：「夫提鼓揮桴，臨難決疑，此將事也。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: When Wu Qi was about to engage in battle his attendants presented him with a sword. Wu Qi said: "To grasp the drum and wield the drumstick, to resolve doubts in the face of danger—these are the affairs of a general.
translations.idiomatic: I note: when Wu Qi was about to fight, attendants offered him a sword. Wu Qi said: "Beating the drum and resolving doubt in battle are a general's business.

sentences.zh: 一劍之任，非將事也。」

translations.literal: The task of a single sword is not the affair of a general."
translations.idiomatic: The work of one sword is not a general's business."

sentences.zh: 謹案諸葛亮臨戎，不親戎服，頓蜀兵於渭南，宣王持劍，卒不敢當。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: When Zhuge Liang faced the army he did not wear military attire himself. He stationed the Shu troops south of the Wei River; Sima Yi held his sword yet in the end did not dare confront him.
translations.idiomatic: I note: Zhuge Liang at the front did not wear armor himself. He held Shu troops south of the Wei River; Sima Yi kept his sword drawn yet dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 此豈弓矢之用也！

translations.literal: Was this the use of bow and arrow!
translations.idiomatic: Was that the use of bow and arrow!

sentences.zh: 謹案楊得意誦長卿之文，武帝曰：「恨不得與此人同時。」

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: When Yang Deyi recited the writings of Sima Xiangru, Emperor Wu said: "How I regret not being a contemporary of this man."
translations.idiomatic: I note: when Yang Deyi recited Sima Xiangru's writing, Emperor Wu said: "I regret not living in the same age as this man."

sentences.zh: 及相如至，終於文園令，不以公卿之位處之者，蓋非其所任故也。

translations.literal: When Xiangru arrived he ended up as Prefect of the Wen Garden and was not placed in a position among the dukes and ministers—presumably because that was not where his talents lay.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangru came he ended as Prefect of the Wen Garden, never raised to ministerial rank—because that was not his proper place.

sentences.zh: 謹案漢法，所舉之主，終身保任。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes the Han law: the master who recommended someone was responsible for guaranteeing them for life.
translations.idiomatic: I note Han law: the recommender guaranteed his candidate for life.

sentences.zh: 楊雄之坐田儀，責其冒薦；

translations.literal: Yang Xiong was implicated because of Tian Yi, held accountable for his reckless recommendation;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong was punished for Tian Yi and held to account for reckless recommendation;

sentences.zh: 成子之居魏相，酬於得賢。

translations.literal: Chengzi's service as Chancellor of Wei was rewarded because he obtained a worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzi's service as Wei chancellor was rewarded because he found a worthy man.

sentences.zh: 賞罰之令行，則請謁之心絕；

translations.literal: When the decrees of reward and punishment are implemented the desire to solicit favors ceases;
translations.idiomatic: When reward and punishment are enforced, solicitation ends;

sentences.zh: 退讓之義著，則貪競之路消。

translations.literal: when the principle of yielding and deference is made clear the path of greed and contention vanishes.
translations.idiomatic: when yielding is honored, greed and rivalry disappear.

sentences.zh: 自然朝廷無爭祿之人，選司有謙捴之士。

translations.literal: Naturally the court will have no men contending for emolument and the selection bureaus will have officials of modest yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Then the court will have no men fighting for salary, and selection offices will have modest officials.

sentences.zh: 仍請寬立年限，容其采訪簡汰，堪用者令其試守，以觀能否；

translations.literal: I further request to leniently set a time limit, allowing investigation and selection and sifting and elimination. Those deemed suitable should be ordered to serve on probation to observe their capability;
translations.idiomatic: I further ask that a generous term be set for inquiry and screening. Suitable men should serve on probation to test ability;

sentences.zh: 參驗行事，以別是非。

translations.literal: verify and examine them through their conduct of affairs to distinguish right from wrong.
translations.idiomatic: and be judged by actual performance to separate right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 不實免王丹之官，得人加翟璜之賞，自然見賢不隱，食祿不專。

translations.literal: For inaccuracy dismiss them from office like Wang Dan; for obtaining a worthy man bestow rewards like Zhai Huang. Naturally seeing worthies they will not conceal them; receiving salary they will not monopolize it.
translations.idiomatic: Fail, and dismiss as Wang Dan was dismissed; succeed, and reward as Zhai Huang was rewarded. Then worthies will not be hidden and salary will not be hoarded.

sentences.zh: 荀彧進鐘繇、郭嘉，劉隱薦李膺、硃穆，勢不雲遠。

translations.literal: Xun Yu recommended Zhong Yao and Guo Jia; Liu Yin recommended Li Ying and Zhu Mu—the precedent is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu advanced Zhong Yao and Guo Jia; Liu Yin recommended Li Ying and Zhu Mu—the examples are near at hand.

sentences.zh: 有稱職者受薦賢之賞，濫舉者抵欺罔之罪，自然舉得賢行，則君子之道長矣。

translations.literal: Let those who recommend worthy men receive the reward for recommending the worthy; let those who make reckless recommendations bear the crime of deception. Naturally if recommendations yield worthy conduct then the way of the gentleman will flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Let successful recommenders receive the reward for finding talent; let reckless recommenders pay the penalty for deceit. Then worthy conduct will spread and the way of the gentleman will grow long.

sentences.zh: 尋轉水部員外郎，累遷給事中、檢校常州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works for Water Control; he rose in succession to Supervising Secretary and acting governor of Chang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice director in the Ministry of Works' water bureau, then rose to Supervising Secretary and acting governor of Chang.

sentences.zh: 屬宣州狂寇硃大目作亂，百姓奔走，謙光嚴備安輯，闔境肅然。

translations.literal: When the mad bandit Zhu Damu of Xuan prefecture rose in rebellion and the people fled in panic, Qian'guang made strict preparations, pacified and settled the region, and the whole jurisdiction became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Zhu Damu of Xuanzhou threw the region into turmoil and the people scattered in panic, Qian'guang tightened defenses, restored order, and the whole circuit grew calm.

sentences.zh: 轉刑部侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫，再遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice, granted the additional title Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally, and was again promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Minister of Justice, received the Silver-Green Tally grand master title, and was later promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，擢拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: During the Jingyun era he was promoted and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun period he was elevated to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時僧惠範恃太平公主權勢，逼奪百姓店肆，州縣不能理。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Huifan relied on the power of Princess Taiping and forcibly seized shops from common people; the prefectures and counties could not deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Huifan, backed by Princess Taiping's influence, seized commoners' shops by force, and local officials could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 謙光將加彈奏，或請寢之，謙光曰：「憲臺理冤滯，何所回避，朝彈暮黜，亦可矣。」

translations.literal: Qian'guang was about to impeach him; some asked that the matter be dropped. Qian'guang said: "The Censorate exists to redress wrongs and delays—what is there to avoid? To be impeached in the morning and dismissed in the evening would be enough."
translations.idiomatic: Qian'guang prepared to impeach him, but others urged him to let the matter drop. He said: "The Censorate exists to clear injustice—why should I shrink back? If I am impeached at dawn and dismissed at dusk, so be it."

sentences.zh: 遂與殿中慕容玽奏彈之，反為太平公主所構，出為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He then joined Palace Censor Murong Ting in submitting an impeachment, but was instead framed by Princess Taiping and sent out as governor of Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He and Palace Censor Murong Ting then jointly impeached Huifan, but Princess Taiping framed him instead, and he was demoted to governor of Qi.

sentences.zh: 惠範既誅，遷太子賓客，轉刑部尚書，加金紫光祿大夫、昭文館學士。

translations.literal: After Huifan was executed, Qian'guang was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then Minister of Justice, and granted the additional titles Grand Master with Gold-Purple Tally and Academician of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After Huifan was put to death, he became Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then Minister of Justice, with the Gold-Purple Tally title and a post as Zhaowen Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為東都留守，又轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he served as Defender of the Eastern Capital, then was again transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he served as Defender of the Eastern Capital, then returned to the post of Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以與太子同名，表請行字，特敕賜名登。

translations.literal: Because he shared the heir apparent's personal name, he submitted a memorial requesting to use his style name; by special edict he was granted the name Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Because his personal name matched the heir apparent's, he memorialized to use his style name instead, and an imperial edict specially granted him the name Deng.

sentences.zh: 尋以孽子悅千牛為憲司所劾，放歸田裏。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because his illegitimate son Yue, a Thousand-Ox Guardsman, was impeached by the censorate, he was released to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his illegitimate son Yue, a Thousand-Ox Guardsman, was impeached by the censorate, and Deng was sent home to his estate.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其家貧，又特給致仕祿。

translations.literal: Because his household was poor, the court specially granted him retirement stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that his family was poor, the court also granted him a special retirement stipend.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，年七十三，贈晉州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died at age seventy-three; posthumously he was made governor of Jin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year at seventy-three; posthumously he was honored as governor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 撰《四時記》二十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Records of the Four Seasons in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Records of the Four Seasons in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 韋湊，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Cou—Wei Cou was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cou came from Wannian in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 曾祖瓚，隋尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zan was Right Vice Director of the Secretariat under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zan served as Sui Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖叔諧，蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuxie was governor of Pu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuxie was governor of Pu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父玄，桂州都督府長史。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was chief administrator of the Guizhou Area Command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan was chief administrator of the Guizhou military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 湊，永淳二年，解褐授婺州參軍，累轉揚府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: Cou, in the second year of Yongchun, left the commoner's garb and was appointed military aide in Wu prefecture; he rose in succession to legal aide in the Yangzhou prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Cou entered service in Yongchun 2 as military aide in Wu prefecture and later became legal aide in the Yangzhou prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 州人前仁壽令孟神爽豪縱，數犯法，交通貴戚，前後官吏莫敢繩按，湊白長史張潛，請因事除之。

translations.literal: A former magistrate of Renshou in the prefecture, Meng Shenshuang, was overbearing and unrestrained, repeatedly violated the law, and had connections with noble kin; officials before and after dared not investigate him. Cou reported to Chief Administrator Zhang Qian and asked to remove him when opportunity arose.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Shenshuang, a former Renshou magistrate in the prefecture, was violent and lawless and cultivated ties with powerful families; no previous official had dared prosecute him. Cou informed Chief Administrator Zhang Qian and asked leave to bring him down when the chance came.

sentences.zh: 會神爽坐事推問，湊無所假借，神爽妄稱有密旨，究問引虛，遂杖殺之，遠近稱伏。

translations.literal: When Shenshuang was implicated in a matter and put to interrogation, Cou showed no leniency; Shenshuang falsely claimed there was a secret edict, but investigation proved the claim empty, and Cou had him beaten to death. Near and far submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenshuang was brought in for questioning, Cou showed no mercy. Shenshuang falsely claimed a secret imperial order protected him, but investigation exposed the lie, and Cou had him beaten to death. People near and far applauded.

sentences.zh: 湊，景龍中歷遷將作少匠、司農少卿。

translations.literal: Cou, during the Jinglong era, rose in succession to Vice Director of Palace Buildings and Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period Cou rose to Vice Director of Palace Buildings and Vice Minister of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 嘗以公事忤宗楚客，出為貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Once, on official business, he offended Zong Chuke and was sent out as governor of Bei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He once clashed with Zong Chuke over official business and was posted out as governor of Bei.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，拜鴻臚少卿，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Cou was appointed Vice Director of the Court for Dependencies and granted the additional title Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, Cou became Vice Director of the Court for Dependencies and received the Silver-Green Tally grand master title.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，轉太府少卿，又兼通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and also concurrently served as Herald for Foreign Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyun 2 he became Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury and also served concurrently as Herald for Foreign Envoys.

sentences.zh: 時改葬節湣太子，優詔加謚；

translations.literal: At that time the Jiemin Crown Prince was being reburied and an edict of special favor added to his posthumous title;
translations.idiomatic: The Jiemin Crown Prince was being reburied, and an edict of special favor enlarged his posthumous title;

sentences.zh: 又雪李多祚等罪，還其官爵，仍議更加贈官。

translations.literal: the crimes of Li Duozuo and others were also cleared, their offices and titles restored, and there was further discussion of adding posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: the convictions of Li Duozuo and others were cleared and their offices restored, while the court also debated further posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 湊上書曰：臣聞王者發號施令，必法乎天道，使三綱攸敘，十等鹹若者，善善明，惡惡著也。

translations.literal: Cou submitted a memorial saying: Your servant has heard that when the king issues commands and decrees, he must model them on the Way of Heaven, so that the three bonds are properly ordered and all ten ranks are thus settled—this is to make good clearly good and evil clearly evil.
translations.idiomatic: Cou submitted a memorial that read: I have heard that when a ruler issues commands and decrees, he must take the Way of Heaven as his model, so that the three bonds are put in order and all ten ranks submit as they should—making good manifest for the good and evil plain for the evil.

sentences.zh: 善善者，懸爵賞以勸之也；

translations.literal: For the good, rank and reward are displayed to encourage them;
translations.idiomatic: For the good, rank and reward are displayed to encourage them;

sentences.zh: 惡惡者，設刑罰以懲之也。

translations.literal: for the evil, punishments are established to chastise them.
translations.idiomatic: for the evil, punishments are established to chastise them.

sentences.zh: 其賞罰所不加者，則考行立謚以褒貶之，所以勸誡將來也。

translations.literal: What reward and punishment cannot reach is judged by conduct and given a posthumous title for praise or blame—this is to admonish those yet to come.
translations.idiomatic: What reward and punishment cannot reach is judged by conduct and given a posthumous title for praise or blame—this is to admonish those yet to come.

sentences.zh: 斯並至公之大猷，非私情之可徇。

translations.literal: All these are great principles of utmost fairness, not matters in which private feeling may be indulged.
translations.idiomatic: All these are great principles of utmost fairness, not matters in which private feeling may be indulged.

sentences.zh: 故箕、微獲用，管、蔡為戮。

translations.literal: Thus Jizi and Weizi were employed, while Guan and Cai were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Jizi and Weizi were employed, while Guan and Cai were executed.

sentences.zh: 謚者，臣議其君，子議其父，而曰「靈」曰「厲」者，不敢以私而亂大猷也，則其餘安可失衷哉！

translations.literal: Posthumous titles are when ministers judge their ruler and sons judge their father—and when one says "Spirit" or "Cruel," one dare not let private feeling disrupt great principles; how then can anything else be allowed to miss the mean!
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous titles are when ministers judge their ruler and sons judge their father—and when one says "Spirit" or "Cruel," one dare not let private feeling disrupt great principles; how then can anything else be allowed to miss the mean!

sentences.zh: 臣竊見節湣太子與李多祚等擁北軍禁旅，上犯宸居，破扉斬關，突禁而入，兵指黃屋，騎騰紫微。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that the Jiemin Crown Prince, together with Li Duozuo and others, led the Northern Army's forbidden troops, ascending to violate the imperial residence—smashing gates and breaking barriers, bursting through the forbidden precinct and entering; weapons pointed at the imperial canopy, horsemen surged within the Purple Forbidden Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has observed that the Jiemin Crown Prince, together with Li Duozuo and others, led the imperial guards of the Northern Army against the imperial residence—breaking down gates and barriers, charging through the forbidden precinct; weapons pointed at the imperial canopy, cavalry surged into the Purple Forbidden Palace.

sentences.zh: 孝和皇帝移禦玄武門，親降德音，諭以逆順，而太子據鞍自若，督眾不停。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaobe moved to the Xuanwu Gate and personally issued an edict of grace, explaining loyalty and rebellion—yet the Heir Apparent sat his saddle at ease and urged his forces on without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaobe moved to the Xuanwu Gate and personally issued an edict of grace, explaining loyalty and rebellion—yet the Heir Apparent sat his saddle at ease and urged his forces on without stopping.

sentences.zh: 俄而其黨悔非，轉逆為順，或回兵討賊，或投狀自拘。

translations.literal: Soon his followers regretted their error and turned rebellion into loyalty—some turned their troops to punish the rebels, others submitted written confessions and restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his followers regretted their error and turned rebellion into loyalty—some turned their troops to punish the rebels, others submitted written confessions and restrained themselves.

sentences.zh: 多祚等伏誅，太子方事逃竄。

translations.literal: Duozuo and others were executed at the place of punishment, and only then did the Heir Apparent set about fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo and others were executed at the place of punishment, and only then did the Heir Apparent set about fleeing.

sentences.zh: 向使同惡相濟，天道無征，賊徒闕倒戈之人，侍臣虧陛戟之衛，其為禍也，胡可忍言！

translations.literal: If the wicked had aided one another and Heaven had offered no sign, if the rebels had lacked men to turn their blades, if attendants had failed in the guard of halberds at the palace steps—what disaster would have ensued is beyond words!
translations.idiomatic: If the wicked had aided one another and Heaven had offered no sign, if the rebels had lacked men to turn their blades, if attendants had failed in the guard of halberds at the palace steps—what disaster would have ensued is beyond words!

sentences.zh: 於時臣任將作少匠，賜通事舍人內供奉。

translations.literal: At that time your subject held the office of Assistant Master of Palace Construction and was granted status as an Inner Attendant Herald.
translations.idiomatic: At that time your subject held the office of Assistant Master of Palace Construction and was granted status as an Inner Attendant Herald.

sentences.zh: 其明日，孝和皇帝引見供奉官等，雨淚謂曰：「幾不與卿等相見！」

translations.literal: The next day Emperor Xiaobe summoned the attendant officials and, with tears streaming down, said: "I almost failed to see you again!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Emperor Xiaobe summoned the attendant officials and, with tears streaming down, said: "I almost failed to see you again!"

sentences.zh: 其為危懼，不亦甚乎！

translations.literal: How extreme the peril and terror were!
translations.idiomatic: How extreme the peril and terror were!

sentences.zh: 而今聖朝雪罪禮葬，謚為節湣，以臣愚識，竊所惑焉。

translations.literal: Yet now the holy dynasty clears their crimes, buries them with ceremony, and gives the posthumous title Jiemin ("Constant and Lamented")—in your subject's foolish understanding, this is privately perplexing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now the holy dynasty clears their crimes, buries them with ceremony, and gives the posthumous title Jiemin ("Constant and Lamented")—in your subject's foolish understanding, this is privately perplexing.

sentences.zh: 夫臣子之禮，嚴敬斯極，故過位必趨，蹙路馬芻有誅。

translations.literal: The rites between minister and ruler reach the utmost in solemn reverence; thus one must quicken one's pace when passing the ruler's place, and even to touch the grass where the ruler's horse passed is punishable by death.
translations.idiomatic: The rites between minister and ruler reach the utmost in solemn reverence; thus one must quicken one's pace when passing the ruler's place, and even to touch the grass where the ruler's horse passed is punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 昔漢成之為太子也，行不敢絕馳道。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng of Han was Heir Apparent, he dared not travel on the imperial carriage road.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng of Han was Heir Apparent, he dared not travel on the imperial carriage road.

sentences.zh: 當周室之衰微也，秦師過周北門，左右免胄而下，王孫滿猶以其不卷甲束兵，譏其無禮，知其必敗。

translations.literal: When the Zhou royal house was in decline, Qin troops passed through the northern gate of Zhou; the attendants doffed their helmets and descended, yet Wangsun Man still reproached them for not rolling up armor and binding their weapons, ridiculed their lack of propriety, and knew they would inevitably be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou royal house was in decline, Qin troops passed through the northern gate of Zhou; the attendants doffed their helmets and descended, yet Wangsun Man still reproached them for not rolling up armor and binding their weapons, ridiculed their lack of propriety, and knew they would inevitably be defeated.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，則太子稱兵宮內，跨馬御前，悖禮已甚矣，況將更甚乎。

translations.literal: From this perspective, for the Heir Apparent to raise troops within the palace and ride his horse before the Emperor—this already transgresses ritual to an extreme; how much more so what actually followed!
translations.idiomatic: From this perspective, for the Heir Apparent to raise troops within the palace and ride his horse before the Emperor—this already transgresses ritual to an extreme; how much more so what actually followed!

sentences.zh: 而可褒謚，此臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: Yet he may be praised with a posthumous title—this your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he may be praised with a posthumous title—this your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 以其斬武三思父子而嘉之乎？

translations.literal: Is it because he beheaded Wu Sansi and his son that he is to be commended?
translations.idiomatic: Is it because he beheaded Wu Sansi and his son that he is to be commended?

sentences.zh: 然弄兵討逆以安君父，則可嘉也，而乃因欲自取之，是競為逆，可褒謚乎？

translations.literal: Yet to wield troops to suppress rebellion and secure lord and father may be praiseworthy; yet because one then wished to seize the throne for oneself, this is competing in rebellion—can he be honored with a posthumous title?
translations.idiomatic: To raise arms against rebels and restore peace to lord and father might be commendable—but to do so because one wished to seize the throne for oneself is to compete in rebellion. Can such a man be honored with a posthumous title?

sentences.zh: 此又臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: This again is what your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 將廢韋氏而嘉之乎？

translations.literal: Is it because he intended to depose Empress Wei that he is to be commended?
translations.idiomatic: Are we to commend him because he intended to depose Empress Wei?

sentences.zh: 然韋氏逆彰義絕，雖誅之亦可也。

translations.literal: Yet when Empress Wei's rebellion was manifest and righteous ties severed, even putting her to death would have been permissible.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wei's rebellion was manifest and all righteous bonds severed, even executing her would have been justified.

sentences.zh: 當此時也，韋氏未有逆彰，未有義絕，於太子為母，豈有廢母之理乎！

translations.literal: At that time Empress Wei's rebellion was not yet manifest, righteous ties were not yet severed, and to the Heir Apparent she was his mother—how could there be any justification for deposing one's mother!
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Empress Wei's treason was not yet plain, no righteous bond had been broken, and to the Heir Apparent she was still his mother—what possible justification could there be for deposing one's own mother!

sentences.zh: 且既非中宗之命而廢之，是劫父廢母，亦悖逆也，可褒謚乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, since she was deposed not by Emperor Zhongzong's command but by coercion, this was coercing the father and deposing the mother—also a perverse rebellion. Can he be honored with a posthumous title?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, she was deposed not by Emperor Zhongzong's order but by force—coercing the father and deposing the mother is itself a grave rebellion. Can he be honored with a posthumous title?

sentences.zh: 此又臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: This again is what your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 夫君或不君，臣安可不臣？

translations.literal: If the lord fails to act as lord, how can the minister fail to act as minister?
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler fails to rule as he should, how can a minister refuse to serve as a minister must?

sentences.zh: 父或不父，子安可不子？

translations.literal: If the father fails to act as father, how can the son fail to act as son?
translations.idiomatic: If a father fails to father as he should, how can a son refuse to be a son must?

sentences.zh: 借如君父有桀、紂之行，臣子無廢殺之理。

translations.literal: Even suppose the lord and father had the conduct of Jie and Zhou, there is no justification for ministers and sons to depose or kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Even if a ruler and father behaved as Jie and Zhou did, ministers and sons still have no warrant to depose or kill him.

sentences.zh: 況先帝功格宇宙，德被生靈，廟號中宗，謚曰孝和皇帝，而逆命之子，可褒謚乎？

translations.literal: How much more so when the late Emperor's achievements reached heaven and earth, his virtue covered all living beings, his temple title is Zhongzong, and his posthumous title is Emperor Xiaobe—and yet a son who defied his command may be honored with a posthumous title?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when the late Emperor's achievements touched heaven and earth, his virtue embraced all living beings, his temple title is Zhongzong, and his posthumous name is Emperor Xiaobe—and a son who defied his command is to be honored with a posthumous title?

sentences.zh: 此又臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: This again is what your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 昔獻公惑驪姬之譖，將殺其太子申生，公子重耳謂之曰：「子盍言子之誌於公乎？」

translations.literal: In antiquity Duke Xian of Jin, deceived by Li Ji's slander, was about to kill his Heir Apparent Shensheng. Prince Chong'er said to him: "Why do you not speak your intentions to the Duke?"
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, Duke Xian of Jin, swayed by Li Ji's slanders, was about to execute his Heir Apparent Shensheng. Prince Chong'er said to him, "Why not declare your intentions to the Duke?"

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「不可，君安驪姬，是我傷君之心也。」

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent said: "I cannot. If my lord is at ease with Li Ji, for me to speak would wound my lord's heart."
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Apparent replied, "I cannot. If my father is content with Li Ji, then for me to speak would only wound his heart."

sentences.zh: 曰：「然則盍行乎？」

translations.literal: He said: "Then why not flee?"
translations.idiomatic: Chong'er asked, "Then why not flee?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不可，君謂我欲弒君也，天下豈有無父之國哉！

translations.literal: He said: "I cannot. My lord would say I wished to assassinate him—and is there any land under Heaven without a father!
translations.idiomatic: Shensheng answered, "I cannot. My father would believe I meant to kill him—and is there any kingdom under Heaven without a father?

sentences.zh: 吾何行之！」

translations.literal: How could I flee!"
translations.idiomatic: How could I flee!"

sentences.zh: 使人辭於狐突曰：「申生不敢愛其死。

translations.literal: He sent someone to take leave of Hu Tu, saying: "Shensheng does not begrudge his death.
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Hu Tu, saying, "Shensheng does not cling to his life.

sentences.zh: 雖然，吾君老矣，子少，國家多難。

translations.literal: Even so, my lord is aged, the heir is young, and the state faces many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my lord is old, the heir is young, and the realm faces many troubles.

sentences.zh: 伯氏茍出而圖吾君，申生受賜而死。」

translations.literal: If you, sir, would go forth and devise plans for my lord, Shensheng will accept the gift of death."
translations.idiomatic: If you, sir, would go forth and counsel my lord, Shensheng will gratefully accept death."

sentences.zh: 再拜稽首，乃自縊。

translations.literal: He bowed twice and touched his head to the ground, then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and touched his forehead to the earth, then hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 其行如是，其謚僅可為恭。

translations.literal: With conduct such as this, his posthumous title could only be Gong ("Respectful").
translations.idiomatic: Conduct such as this merited a posthumous title no higher than Gong ("Respectful").

sentences.zh: 今太子之行反是，可謚為節湣乎？

translations.literal: Today the Heir Apparent's conduct is the opposite of this—can he be given the posthumous title Jiemin?
translations.idiomatic: The present Heir Apparent's conduct was the very reverse—can he be given the posthumous title Jiemin?

sentences.zh: 此又臣所未諭也。

translations.literal: This again is what your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, your subject cannot comprehend.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝末年，江充與太子有隙，恐帝晏駕後為太子所誅。

translations.literal: In the final years of Emperor Wu of Han, Jiang Chong had a rift with the Heir Apparent and feared that after the Emperor's death he would be executed by the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Emperor Wu of Han, Jiang Chong quarreled with the Heir Apparent and feared that once the Emperor died, the Heir Apparent would have him executed.

sentences.zh: 會巫蠱事起，充典理其事。

translations.literal: When the witchcraft scandal arose, Chong was put in charge of investigating it.
translations.idiomatic: When the witchcraft affair broke out, Chong was assigned to investigate it.

sentences.zh: 因此為奸，遂至太子宮掘蠱，得桐木以誣太子。

translations.literal: Seizing this opportunity for treachery, he went so far as to dig for witchcraft effigies in the Heir Apparent's palace and obtained paulownia wood to frame the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting the occasion for treachery, he dug for witchcraft dolls in the Heir Apparent's palace and planted paulownia wood to incriminate him.

sentences.zh: 時武帝避暑甘泉宮，獨皇后、太子在，太子不能自明，納其少傅石德謀，遂矯節斬充，因敗逃匿。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu was summering at Ganquan Palace; only the Empress and Heir Apparent remained at the capital. Unable to clear himself, the Heir Apparent adopted the counsel of his Junior Tutor Shi De, forged an imperial credential to behead Chong, and upon defeat fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was then at his summer retreat in Ganquan Palace, leaving only the Empress and Heir Apparent in the capital. Unable to prove his innocence, the Heir Apparent followed the advice of his Junior Tutor Shi De, forged an imperial warrant to execute Chong, and after defeat fled into hiding.

sentences.zh: 非稱兵詣闕，無逆謀於父，然身死於湖，不葬無謚。

translations.literal: He did not raise troops and march to the palace gate, nor did he harbor rebellious designs against his father—yet he died at Lake, was buried without ceremony, and received no posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: He did not raise an army and march on the palace, nor did he plot rebellion against his father—yet he died at Lake, was buried without honor, and received no posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 至昭帝時，有男子詣北闕自稱衛太子，制使公卿識視，至者莫敢發言。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhao, a man came to the northern gate and proclaimed himself the Wei Heir Apparent. An edict ordered the high ministers to examine and identify him; those who arrived dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhao, a man appeared at the northern gate claiming to be the Wei Heir Apparent. An edict commanded the chief ministers to identify him, but none who came dared speak.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹雋不疑後至，叱從吏收縛之。

translations.literal: The Commandant of Jingzhao, Juan Buyi, arrived later and rebuked his attendant officers to seize and bind him.
translations.idiomatic: Juan Buyi, Commandant of Jingzhao, arrived last and ordered his attendants to seize and bind the man.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「是非未可知，且安之。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "Whether this is true or false is not yet known—leave him be for now."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged, "We cannot yet know whether this is true—let us hold him for now."

sentences.zh: 不疑曰：「諸君何患於衛太子。

translations.literal: Buyi said: "What do you gentlemen fear from the Wei Heir Apparent?
translations.idiomatic: Buyi replied, "What do you fear from the Wei Heir Apparent?

sentences.zh: 昔蒯聵出奔，輒拒而不納，《春秋》是之。

translations.literal: In antiquity Kuai Kui fled into exile, and Zhe refused to admit him—the Spring and Autumn Annals approves of this.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Kuai Kui fled into exile and Zhe refused to receive him—the Spring and Autumn Annals commends this.

sentences.zh: 衛太子得罪先帝，亡不即死，今來自詣，此罪人也。」

translations.literal: The Wei Heir Apparent offended the late Emperor, fled without accepting death at once, and now has come of his own accord—this man is a criminal."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Heir Apparent wronged the late Emperor, fled instead of accepting death, and now presents himself of his own accord—he is a criminal."

sentences.zh: 遂送制獄。

translations.literal: He was then sent to the prisons of the imperial secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The man was sent to the imperial prisons.

sentences.zh: 天子聞而嘉之曰：「公卿大臣，當用經術明於大義者。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven heard of this and commended him, saying: "Ministers and great officials ought to be men versed in the classics and clear on great principles."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard and praised him, saying, "Ministers and high officials should be men learned in the classics and clear on great principles."

sentences.zh: 及後太子孫立為天子，是曰孝宣皇帝，太子方獲禮葬，而謚曰戾。

translations.literal: Later, when the Heir Apparent's grandson ascended as Son of Heaven—the man known as Emperor Xiaoxuan—the Heir Apparent at last received ceremonial burial, and his posthumous title was Li ("Unruly").
translations.idiomatic: Only later, when the Heir Apparent's grandson ascended the throne as Emperor Xiaoxuan, did the Heir Apparent receive proper burial—and his posthumous title was Li ("Unruly").

sentences.zh: 今節湣太子之行比之，豈可同年而語。
