translations.literal: Qiuli seized on the matter and impeached him, saying: "These misled people, in recent times, had no good officials to instruct them; their walls were not secure; driven by the bandits, they sought only to preserve themselves—how could they have harbored rebellion from the first!
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli impeached him, saying: "These people were misled. They had no good officials to guide them, their defenses were weak, and the rebels drove them to save themselves—how can they be said to have harbored treason from the start?

sentences.zh: 懿宗擁強兵數十萬，聞賊將至，走保城邑，罪當誅戮。

translations.literal: Wuyizong held several hundred thousand strong troops; when he heard the bandits were coming, he fled to defend walled towns—his crime deserves execution.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyizong commanded hundreds of thousands of troops, yet fled to walled towns when he heard the enemy approach—his crime deserves death.

sentences.zh: 今乃移禍於詿誤之人，豈是為臣之道？

translations.literal: Now he shifts the blame onto misled people—is this the way of a minister?
translations.idiomatic: Now he shifts blame onto the misled—is that the conduct of a minister?

sentences.zh: 請斬懿宗以謝河北百姓。」

translations.literal: I ask that Wuyizong be beheaded to answer to the people of Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Wuyizong be beheaded to answer to the people of Hebei."

sentences.zh: 懿宗大懼，則天竟降制赦之。

translations.literal: Wuyizong was greatly afraid, and Empress Wu ultimately issued an edict pardoning them.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyizong was terrified, and Empress Wu ultimately issued an edict pardoning the people.

sentences.zh: 契丹陷幽州，饋輓不給，左相豆盧欽望請輟京官兩月俸料以助軍，求禮謂欽望曰：「公祿厚俸優，輟之可也。

translations.literal: When the Khitan captured You prefecture and supplies could not be delivered, Left Chief Minister Dou Lu Qinwang asked that capital officials forgo two months' salary to aid the army. Qiuli said to Qinwang: "Your salary and stipend are generous; you may forgo them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan captured Youzhou and supplies failed, Left Chief Minister Dou Lu Qinwang proposed that capital officials forgo two months' salary for the army. Qiuli told him: "Your salary is generous—you may forgo it.

sentences.zh: 國家富有四海，足以儲軍國之用，何藉貧官薄俸。

translations.literal: The state is rich within the four seas and has enough to store for military and state use—why rely on the meager salaries of poor officials?
translations.idiomatic: The state is rich within the four seas and can supply military needs—why take from poor officials' thin salaries?

sentences.zh: 公此舉豈宰相法邪？」

translations.literal: Is this proposal of yours the way of a chief minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this the way of a chief minister?"

sentences.zh: 欽望作色拒之，乃奏曰：「秦、漢皆有稅算以贍軍，求禮不識大體，妄有訟辭。」

translations.literal: Qinwang changed color and rejected him, then memorialized, saying: "Qin and Han both levied taxes to supply the army; Qiuli does not understand the larger principle and rashly disputes the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang flushed with anger and rejected him, then memorialized, saying, "Qin and Han had levied taxes to supply armies; Qiuli does not understand larger principles and rashly disputed the matter."

sentences.zh: 求禮對曰：「秦皇、漢武稅天下，虛中以事邊，奈何使聖朝則效？

translations.literal: Qiuli replied, saying: "The First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han taxed the empire and emptied the center to serve the frontier—how can the sage dynasty be made to imitate them?
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli replied: "The First Emperor and Emperor Wu taxed the empire and emptied the center to serve the frontier—must our sage dynasty imitate them?

sentences.zh: 不知欽望此言是大體耶！」

translations.literal: Does Qinwang not know whether his words accord with the larger principle!"
translations.idiomatic: Does Qinwang not know whether his words accord with larger principles?"

sentences.zh: 事遂不行。

translations.literal: The matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 時三月雪，鳳閣侍郎蘇味道等以為瑞，草表將賀，求禮止之曰：「宰相調燮陰陽，而致雪降暮春，災也，安得為瑞？

translations.literal: At the time snow fell in the third month; Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Su Weidao and others took it as an auspicious sign and drafted a memorial of congratulation. Qiuli stopped them, saying: "Chief ministers harmonize yin and yang, yet snow falls in late spring—this is a calamity; how can it be an auspicious sign?
translations.idiomatic: Snow fell in the third month. Vice Minister Su Weidao and others took it as an omen of good fortune and drafted a congratulatory memorial. Qiuli stopped them: "Chief ministers harmonize yin and yang, yet snow falls in late spring—that is a calamity, not a blessing.

sentences.zh: 如三月雪為瑞雪，則臘月雷亦瑞雷也。」

translations.literal: If snow in the third month is auspicious snow, then thunder in the twelfth month is also auspicious thunder."
translations.idiomatic: If snow in the third month is auspicious, then thunder in the twelfth month is auspicious too."

sentences.zh: 舉朝嗤笑，以為口實。

translations.literal: The whole court laughed and took it as a byword.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court laughed and made it a byword.

sentences.zh: 求禮竟以剛正，名位不達而卒。

translations.literal: Qiuli, because of his stern uprightness, never attained high rank and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli never rose high in rank because of his stern uprightness and died without attaining great office.

sentences.zh: 辛替否，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Xin Tifou—Xin Tifou was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Tifou came from the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 景龍年為左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong years he served as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period he served as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 時中宗置公主府官屬，安樂公主府所補尤多猥濫。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Zhongzong established official staffs for princesses' households; appointments in Princess Anle's household were especially numerous and lax.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong had established official staffs for princesses' households, and appointments in Princess Anle's household were especially numerous and improper.

sentences.zh: 又駙馬武崇訓死後，棄舊宅別造一宅，侈麗過甚。

translations.literal: Moreover, after the death of her consort Wu Chongxun, she abandoned the old residence and built another, excessively lavish.
translations.idiomatic: After her consort Wu Chongxun died, she abandoned their old residence and built another of excessive splendor.

sentences.zh: 時又盛興佛寺，百姓勞弊，帑藏為之空竭。

translations.literal: At the time Buddhist temples were also greatly promoted; the common people were worn out with labor, and the treasury was emptied for it.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist temples were also being built on a vast scale, exhausting the people and emptying the treasury.

sentences.zh: 替否上疏諫曰：臣聞古之建官，員不必備，九卿以下，皆有其位而闕其選。

translations.literal: Xin Tifou submitted a memorial in remonstrance, saying: Your servant has heard that in ancient times when establishing offices, the complement of officials need not be full; below the Nine Ministers, all had their positions but selections were left vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Tifou submitted a memorial of remonstrance that read: I have heard that in ancient times when offices were established, posts need not be fully filled; below the Nine Ministers, positions existed but appointments were often left vacant.

sentences.zh: 賞一人謀乎三事，職一人訪乎群司，負寵者畏權勢之在躬，知榮者避權門而不入。

translations.literal: Rewarding one person consulted three affairs; appointing one person inquired of the various departments. Those bearing favor feared power and influence resting on themselves; those knowing honor avoided powerful families and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: To reward one man, three matters were weighed; to appoint one man, all departments were consulted. Favorites feared power concentrated in their own hands; men of honor shunned powerful cliques and kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 故稱賞不僭，官不濫，士皆完行，家有廉節，朝廷有餘俸，百姓有餘食。

translations.literal: Therefore it was said rewards were not excessive, offices were not overfilled, scholars all maintained complete conduct, families had incorruptible integrity, the court had surplus salaries, and the common people had surplus food.
translations.idiomatic: Thus rewards were not excessive and offices were not overfilled; scholars kept their integrity, households maintained frugality, the court had surplus pay, and the people had surplus food.

sentences.zh: 下忠於上，上禮於下，委裘而無倉卒之危，垂拱而無顛沛之患。

translations.literal: The lower levels were loyal to superiors; superiors treated the lower levels with propriety. Robes were entrusted without sudden danger; hands were folded in governance without the calamity of upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects were loyal below and rulers were courteous above; the throne could be entrusted without sudden peril, and governance could proceed at ease without crisis.

sentences.zh: 夫事有惕耳目，動心慮，作不師古，以行於今者，蓋有之矣。

translations.literal: Affairs that startle the ears and eyes and stir the heart and mind, undertaken not following antiquity yet practiced today—such things indeed exist.
translations.idiomatic: There are indeed affairs that shock the senses and disturb the mind, conducted without following antiquity yet carried out today.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下百倍行賞，十倍增官，金銀不供其印，束帛無充於錫，何愧於無用之臣，何慚於無力之士！

translations.literal: I consider that Your Majesty rewards a hundredfold and increases offices tenfold; gold and silver cannot supply the seals, bolts of silk are insufficient for gifts—what shame before useless ministers, what embarrassment before powerless scholars!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rewards a hundredfold and multiplies offices tenfold; gold and silver cannot supply the seals, and silk cannot fill the gifts—what shame is there before useless ministers, what embarrassment before powerless men of talent!

sentences.zh: 至於公府補授，罕有推擇，遂使富商豪賈，盡居纓冕之流，鬻伎行巫，鹹涉膏腴之地。

translations.literal: As for appointments and commissions in the public offices, rarely is there proper selection, thus causing rich merchants and powerful traders all to join the ranks of the capped and robed, and sellers of skills and practicing shamans all to tread upon fertile lands.
translations.idiomatic: As for public appointments, proper selection is rare, so wealthy merchants occupy official ranks and sellers of skills and practitioners of sorcery all gain fertile lands.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古人曰：「福生有基，禍生有胎。」

translations.literal: Your servant has heard the ancients say: "Blessedness has its foundation; calamity has its embryo."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard the ancients say: "Blessings have their foundation; disasters have their beginnings."

sentences.zh: 伏惟公主陛下之愛女，選賢良以嫁之，設官職以輔之，傾府庫以賜之，壯第觀以居之，廣池膋以嬉之，可謂之至重也，可謂之至憐也。

translations.literal: I consider the princess is Your Majesty's beloved daughter: selecting the worthy and good to marry her, establishing official posts to assist her, emptying the treasury to bestow upon her, building magnificent residences for her to dwell in, broadening ponds and gardens for her to play in—this can be called the utmost importance, can be called the utmost affection.
translations.idiomatic: The princess is Your Majesty's beloved daughter: worthy men were chosen for her marriage, officials were appointed to assist her, the treasury was emptied to endow her, grand mansions were built for her residence, and broad ponds and gardens were made for her pleasure—this is utmost favor, utmost tenderness.

sentences.zh: 然而用不合於古義，行不根於人心，將恐變愛成憎，轉福為禍。

translations.literal: However, the practice does not accord with ancient righteousness, the conduct is not rooted in the people's hearts; I fear love will turn to hatred and blessing will transform into calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the practice does not accord with ancient principle, and the conduct is not rooted in popular sentiment; I fear love will turn to hatred and blessing into disaster.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 竭人之力，人怨也；

translations.literal: Exhausting people's strength causes their resentment;
translations.idiomatic: Exhausting people's strength breeds resentment;

sentences.zh: 費人之財，人怨也；

translations.literal: Expending people's wealth causes their resentment;
translations.idiomatic: Expending people's wealth breeds resentment;

sentences.zh: 奪人之家，人怨也。

translations.literal: Seizing people's homes causes their resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing people's homes breeds resentment.

sentences.zh: 愛數子而取三怨於天下，使邊疆之士不盡力，朝廷之士不盡忠，人之散矣，獨持所愛，何所恃乎？

translations.literal: Loving a few children and incurring three resentments from the empire causes officers on the frontiers not to exert full strength and officers at court not to show full loyalty—the people are scattered; alone holding what one loves, what can one rely upon?
translations.idiomatic: To love a few children while incurring three resentments under Heaven is to leave frontier soldiers unwilling to exert themselves and court officials unwilling to serve loyally; when the people are scattered, what can Your Majesty rely upon by clinging only to those you favor?

sentences.zh: 向者魯王賞同諸婿，禮等朝臣，則亦有今日之福，無曩時之禍。

translations.literal: Previously, if the Prince of Lu's rewards were equal to those of the other sons-in-law and his ceremonies equal to court ministers, then there would also be today's blessings, not the disasters of former times.
translations.idiomatic: If previously the Prince of Lu's rewards had equaled those of the other sons-in-law and his ceremonial standing that of court ministers, there would be today's blessings without yesterday's disasters.

sentences.zh: 人徒見其禍，不知禍之所來。

translations.literal: People only see the disaster, not knowing whence the disaster came.
translations.idiomatic: People see only the disaster, not the source from which it came.

sentences.zh: 所以禍者，寵愛過於臣子也。

translations.literal: The reason for the disaster is that favor and love exceeded that for ministers and sons.
translations.idiomatic: The reason for the disaster is that favor exceeded what is due to ministers and sons.

sentences.zh: 去年七月五日，已見其征矣。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the seventh month last year, its portent was already seen.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the seventh month last year, the portent was already visible.

sentences.zh: 而今事無改，更尚因循，棄一宅而造一宅，忘前禍而忽後禍。

translations.literal: Yet now affairs are unchanged, moreover still following the old ways, abandoning one residence to build another, forgetting the former disaster and neglecting the later one.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now nothing has changed; the old course is still followed—one residence is abandoned to build another, the former disaster forgotten and the coming one ignored.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂陛下憎之矣，非愛之也。

translations.literal: Your servant privately believes Your Majesty hates her, not loves her.
translations.idiomatic: I privately believe Your Majesty hates her rather than loves her.

sentences.zh: 臣聞君以人為本，本固則邦寧。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the sovereign takes the people as his foundation; when the foundation is secure, the state is tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the ruler takes the people as his foundation; when the foundation is secure, the state is at peace.

sentences.zh: 邦寧則陛下夫婦、母子長相保也。

translations.literal: When the state is tranquil, then Your Majesty, husband and wife, mother and son, may long preserve one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the state is at peace, Your Majesty, husband and wife, mother and son, may long preserve one another.

sentences.zh: 伏惟外謀宰臣，為久安之計以存之，不使奸臣賊子以伺之。

translations.literal: I humbly beseech you to consult with ministers of state externally, to devise plans for lasting peace in order to preserve it, and not to allow treacherous ministers and villainous sons to lie in wait.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that Your Majesty consult your chief ministers and devise a plan for lasting security, so that treacherous ministers and wicked sons may not lie in wait.

sentences.zh: 臣聞微不可不防，遠不可不慮。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the subtle must be guarded against and the distant must be considered.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that what is subtle must be guarded against and what is distant must be considered.

sentences.zh: 當今疆場危駭，倉廩空虛，揭竿守禦之士賞不及，肝腦塗地之卒輸不充。

translations.literal: At present the borders are in peril and alarm, the granaries are empty and depleted; those who raise spears in defense are not rewarded, and provisions for troops who spill their brains upon the ground are insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: At present the frontiers are in alarm, the granaries are empty; defenders who take up arms go unrewarded, and supplies for soldiers who spill their blood on the field are insufficient.

sentences.zh: 而方大起寺舍，廣造第宅，伐木空山，不足充梁棟，運土塞路，不足充墻壁。

translations.literal: Yet now on a grand scale you are building monasteries and temples and extensively constructing mansions, felling trees until mountains are bare yet insufficient to fill beams and pillars, transporting earth until roads are blocked yet insufficient to fill walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yet temples and mansions are being built on a vast scale—trees are felled until mountains are bare, yet not enough for beams and pillars; earth is moved until roads are blocked, yet not enough for walls.

sentences.zh: 誇古耀今，逾章越制，百僚鉗口四海傷心。

translations.literal: You boast of antiquity and dazzle the present, exceeding regulations and overstepping institutions, causing all officials to remain silent and the whole realm to grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Boasting of antiquity while outshining the present, exceeding regulations and overstepping institutions—all officials are silenced and the whole realm grieves.

sentences.zh: 夫釋教者，以清凈為基，慈悲為主，故當體道以濟物，不欲利己以損人，故常去己以全真，不為榮身以害教。

translations.literal: Now the Buddhist teaching takes purity and stillness as its basis and compassion as its guiding principle; therefore it should embody the Way to succor beings and not desire to benefit oneself at others' expense; thus it constantly abandons the self to preserve the true and does not seek to glorify the body to the detriment of the teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist teaching takes purity and stillness as its foundation and compassion as its principle; it should embody the Way to succor beings, not benefit oneself at others' expense, abandon the self to preserve truth, and not glorify the body to the harm of the teaching.

sentences.zh: 三時之月，掘山穿池，損命也；

translations.literal: In the three seasons of the year, digging into mountains and piercing ponds harms life;
translations.idiomatic: In the three seasons, digging mountains and excavating ponds harms life;

sentences.zh: 殫府虛帑，損人也；

translations.literal: Exhausting the treasury and depleting stores harms the people;
translations.idiomatic: Emptying the treasury harms the people;

sentences.zh: 廣殿長廊，榮身也。

translations.literal: Grand halls and long corridors glorify the body.
translations.idiomatic: Grand halls and long corridors glorify the self.

sentences.zh: 損命則不慈悲，損人則不濟物，榮身則不清凈，豈大聖大神之心乎！

translations.literal: To harm life is not compassionate; to harm people is not to succor beings; to glorify the body is not pure and still—is this the heart of the great sages and divine beings!
translations.idiomatic: To harm life is not compassion; to harm people is not succoring beings; to glorify the self is not purity—is this the mind of the great sage!

sentences.zh: 臣以為非真教，非佛意，違時行，違人欲。

translations.literal: Your servant believes this is not the true teaching, not the Buddha's intent; it contravenes the times and opposes human desires.
translations.idiomatic: I believe this is not the true teaching, not the Buddha's intent; it goes against the times and against what people desire.

sentences.zh: 自像王西下，佛教東傳，青螺不入於周前，白馬方行於漢後。

translations.literal: Since the Image King descended in the west and the Buddhist teaching spread eastward, the green snail did not enter before the Zhou, and the White Horse only traveled after the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Buddha descended in the west and Buddhism spread eastward, it did not enter before the Zhou, and the White Horse only came after the Han.

sentences.zh: 風流雨散，千帝百王，飾彌盛而國彌空，役彌重而禍彌大。

translations.literal: Like wind scattering and rain dispersing, through a thousand emperors and a hundred kings, adornment grew more lavish while the state grew emptier, labors grew heavier while calamities grew greater.
translations.idiomatic: Through a thousand emperors and a hundred kings, ornament grew ever more lavish while states grew ever emptier, labor ever heavier while disasters ever greater.

sentences.zh: 覆車繼軌，曾不改途，晉臣以佞佛取譏，梁主以舍身構隙。

translations.literal: Overturned carts followed in the tracks yet the path was never altered; Jin ministers were ridiculed for flattering Buddha, and the Liang sovereign brought about strife by sacrificing his body.
translations.idiomatic: Overturned carts followed one after another yet the course was never changed; Jin ministers were mocked for fawning on Buddhism, and the Liang ruler brought strife by sacrificing his body.

sentences.zh: 若以造寺必為其理體，養人不足以經邦，則殷、周已往皆暗亂，漢、魏已降皆聖明；

translations.literal: If building temples is necessarily the embodiment of principle and nourishing the people is insufficient to govern the state, then the Yin and Zhou and those before were all benighted and chaotic, while the Han, Wei and those after were all sagely and enlightened;
translations.idiomatic: If building temples is necessarily the embodiment of principle and nourishing the people is insufficient to govern the state, then Yin and Zhou and all before were benighted and chaotic, while Han, Wei and all after were sagely and enlightened;

sentences.zh: 殷、周已往為不長，漢、魏已降為不短。

translations.literal: The Yin and Zhou and those before were not long-lasting, while the Han, Wei and those after were not short-lived.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Zhou and all before did not endure long, while Han, Wei and all after did not fall short in duration.

sentences.zh: 臣聞夏為天子二十餘代而殷受之，殷為天子二十餘代而周受之，周為天子三十餘代而秦受之，自漢已後歷代可知也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Xia held the Son of Heaven's mandate for over twenty generations before Yin received it; Yin held it for over twenty generations before Zhou received it; Zhou held it for over thirty generations before Qin received it; from Han onward the succession of dynasties can be known.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Xia ruled for over twenty generations before Yin succeeded, Yin for over twenty generations before Zhou, Zhou for over thirty before Qin; from Han onward the succession is known.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 有道之長，無道之短，豈因其窮金玉、修塔廟，方得久長之祚乎！

translations.literal: Those with the Way endured long; those without the Way were short-lived. How could it be because they exhausted gold and jade and built pagodas and temples that they obtained long-lasting reigns!
translations.idiomatic: Those who had the Way endured long; those without it were short-lived. How could exhausting gold and jade and building pagodas and temples alone secure a long reign!

sentences.zh: 臣聞於經曰：「菩薩心住於法而行布施，如人入暗，即無所見。」

translations.literal: Your servant has heard in the sutras: "When a bodhisattva's mind abides in dharmas while practicing giving, it is like a person entering darkness—they see nothing."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard in the sutras: "When a bodhisattva's mind abides in dharmas while practicing giving, it is like a person entering darkness who sees nothing."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「一切有為法，如夢幻泡影，如露亦如電。」

translations.literal: It is also said: "All conditioned dharmas are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows; like dew and like lightning."
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "All conditioned phenomena are like dreams, illusions, bubbles, shadows, like dew and like lightning."

sentences.zh: 臣以減雕琢之費以賑貧下，是有如來之德；

translations.literal: Your servant believes that reducing the expense of carving and ornamentation to relieve the poor and lowly would be to possess the virtue of the Tathagata;
translations.idiomatic: To reduce carving and ornamentation and relieve the poor would be to possess the Tathagata's virtue;

sentences.zh: 息穿掘之苦以全昆蟲，是有如來之仁；

translations.literal: Ceasing the suffering of digging and piercing to preserve insects and creatures would be to possess the compassion of the Tathagata;
translations.idiomatic: To cease digging and piercing and preserve insects would be to possess the Tathagata's compassion;

sentences.zh: 罷營構之直以給邊陲，是有湯、武之功；

translations.literal: Halting funds for construction to supply the border regions would be to possess the merit of Tang and Wu;
translations.idiomatic: To halt construction funds and supply the frontiers would be to possess the merit of Tang and Wu;

sentences.zh: 回不急之祿以購廉清，是有唐、虞之理。

translations.literal: Redirecting unnecessary emoluments to purchase integrity and purity would be to possess the governance of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: To redirect unnecessary salaries to reward integrity and purity would be to possess the governance of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 陛下緩其所急，急其所緩，親未來而疏見在，失真實而冀虛無，重俗人之所為而輕天子之功業，臣竊痛之矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty relaxes what is urgent and hastens what is relaxed; you draw close to the future and distance the present, lose the real and hope for the void, value what common people do and belittle the Son of Heaven's achievements—your servant privately grieves over this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty relaxes what is urgent and presses what is relaxed, draws near to the future and distances the present, loses what is real and hopes for the void, values what common people do and belittles the Son of Heaven's achievements—I grieve over this.

sentences.zh: 當今出財依勢者盡度為沙門，避役奸訛者盡度為沙門；

translations.literal: At present those with wealth and influence all take monastic vows to become monks, and those evading service through deceit and falsehood all take vows to become monks;
translations.idiomatic: At present those with wealth and influence all take vows to become monks, and those evading service through fraud all take vows to become monks;

sentences.zh: 其所未度，唯貧窮與善人。

translations.literal: Those who have not yet taken vows are only the poor and the good.
translations.idiomatic: Those not yet ordained are only the poor and the good.

sentences.zh: 將何以作範乎？

translations.literal: How then shall models be established?
translations.idiomatic: How then will a model be set?

sentences.zh: 將何以役力乎？

translations.literal: How then shall labor be employed?
translations.idiomatic: How then will labor be mobilized?

sentences.zh: 臣以為出家者，舍塵俗，離朋黨，無私愛。

translations.literal: Your servant believes that those who leave the household life abandon worldly dust, leave behind factions, and have no private attachments.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that those who leave the household abandon worldly affairs, leave factions behind, and have no private attachments.

sentences.zh: 今殖貨營生，非舍塵俗；

translations.literal: Now accumulating goods and pursuing livelihood is not abandoning worldly dust;
translations.idiomatic: Now accumulating goods and pursuing livelihood is not abandoning worldly affairs;

sentences.zh: 拔親樹知，非離朋黨；

translations.literal: Promoting relatives and establishing acquaintances is not leaving behind factions;
translations.idiomatic: Promoting relatives and cultivating connections is not leaving factions;

sentences.zh: 畜妻養孥，非無私愛。

translations.literal: Keeping wives and nurturing children is not having no private attachments.
translations.idiomatic: Keeping wives and raising children is not being free of private attachments.

sentences.zh: 是致人以毀道，非廣道以求人。

translations.literal: This leads people to destroy the Way; it is not broadening the Way to seek people.
translations.idiomatic: This leads people to destroy the Way rather than broadening the Way to attract people.

sentences.zh: 伏見今之宮觀臺榭，京師之與洛陽，不增修飾，猶恐奢麗。

translations.literal: I humbly observe that the palaces, observatories, terraces, and pavilions in the capital and in Luoyang, if not further adorned, would still be feared as extravagant and lavish.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that the palaces, observatories, terraces, and pavilions in the capital and Luoyang, even without further adornment, would still be feared as extravagant.

sentences.zh: 陛下尚欲填池塹，捐苑囿，以賑貧人無產業者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty still desires to fill in moats and ponds and relinquish parks and enclosures to relieve the poor who have no property.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty still wishes to fill moats and ponds and relinquish parks to relieve the poor who have no property.

sentences.zh: 今天下之寺蓋無其數，一寺當陛下一宮，壯麗之甚矣！

translations.literal: Now the monasteries in the realm are beyond count; one monastery equals one palace of Your Majesty—how exceedingly magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: The monasteries under Heaven are beyond count; one monastery equals one of Your Majesty's palaces—how exceedingly magnificent!

sentences.zh: 用度過之矣！

translations.literal: The expenditure exceeds it!
translations.idiomatic: The expenditure exceeds even that!

sentences.zh: 是十分天下之財而佛有七八，陛下何有之矣！

translations.literal: This is seven or eight parts out of ten of the realm's wealth belonging to Buddha—what then does Your Majesty possess!
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight parts in ten of the realm's wealth belong to Buddhism—what then does Your Majesty possess!

sentences.zh: 百姓何食之矣！

translations.literal: What then do the common people eat!
translations.idiomatic: What then do the common people eat!

sentences.zh: 雖以陰陽為炭，萬物為銅，役不食之人，使不衣之士，猶尚不給。

translations.literal: Even if you took yin and yang as charcoal and all things as copper, employing people who do not eat and using men who do not wear clothes, it would still be insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Even if yin and yang were used as charcoal and all things as copper, employing men who do not eat and using men who do not wear clothes, it would still not suffice.

sentences.zh: 況資於天生地養，風動雨潤，而後得之乎！

translations.literal: How much more so when relying on what is born of heaven and nurtured by earth, moved by wind and moistened by rain, before it can be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: How much less when wealth depends on what heaven and earth produce, moved by wind and moistened by rain!

sentences.zh: 臣聞國無九年之儲，國非其國。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that if a state does not have a store for nine years, it is not a state.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a state without nine years' stores is not truly a state.

sentences.zh: 伏計倉廩，度府庫，百僚供給，百事用度，臣恐卒歲不充，況九年之積乎！

translations.literal: I humbly calculate the granaries, measure the treasury stores, the provisions for all officials, the expenses for all affairs—your servant fears they will not suffice for a single year's end, let alone an accumulation for nine years!
translations.idiomatic: Calculating the granaries and measuring the treasuries, with provisions for all officials and expenses for all affairs, I fear they will not suffice for one year's end, let alone nine years' accumulation!

sentences.zh: 一旦風塵再擾，霜雹薦臻，沙門不可擐干戈，寺塔不足攘饑饉，臣竊痛之矣！

translations.literal: Should the winds of war once again stir or frost and hail repeatedly arrive, monks cannot grasp shield and spear; monasteries and pagodas cannot ward off famine—your servant privately grieves over this!
translations.idiomatic: Should war arise again or frost and hail repeatedly strike, monks cannot take up arms and monasteries cannot ward off famine—I grieve over this!

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，安樂公主被誅。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Princess Anle was executed.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later, Princess Anle was executed.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，又為金仙、玉真公主廣營二觀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, construction was again expanded on the two monasteries for the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected princesses.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, construction again expanded on the two monasteries for the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected princesses.

sentences.zh: 先是，中宗時斜封受官人一切停任，凡數百千人，又有敕放令卻上。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the time of Emperor Zhongzong, all those who had received office through irregular sealed appointments had been dismissed—several hundred or a thousand in all—and there was also an edict releasing them to return to office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under Emperor Zhongzong, all who had received office through irregular sealed appointments had been dismissed—several hundred or more—and an edict then allowed them to return.

sentences.zh: 替否時為左補闕，又上疏陳時政曰：臣嘗以為古之用度不時，爵賞不當，破家亡國者，口說不如身逢，耳聞不如眼見，臣請以有唐已來理國之得失，陛下之所眼見者以言之。

translations.literal: Xin Tifou was then Left Remonstrator and again submitted a memorial setting forth current policy, saying: Your servant has often considered that in ancient times those whose expenditures were untimely and whose conferral of ranks and rewards was improper, leading to the ruin of families and loss of states—spoken words are not as good as personally encountering, hearing with the ear is not as good as seeing with the eye. Your servant requests to speak using the successes and failures in governing the state since the Tang dynasty began, which Your Majesty has seen with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Tifou was then Left Remonstrator and again memorialized on current policy, saying: I have often thought that in ancient times, untimely expenditure and improper ranks and rewards brought ruin to families and states—hearing is not as good as seeing. I ask to speak of the successes and failures in governing since Tang began, which Your Majesty has seen with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下審之聽之，擇善而從之，則萬歲之業，自可致矣，何憂乎黎庶之不康，福祚之不永！

translations.literal: If only Your Majesty would examine and listen to this, choosing the good and following it, then the enterprise of ten thousand years could naturally be achieved. Why worry that the common people will not prosper or that the felicitous reign will not be long-lasting!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty examines and listens, choosing the good and following it, the enterprise of ten thousand years can naturally be achieved. Why worry that the people will not prosper or that fortune will not endure!

sentences.zh: 伏以太宗文武聖皇帝，陛下之祖，撥亂反正，開階立極，得至理之體，設簡要之方。

translations.literal: I humbly submit that Emperor Taizong, the Civil and Martial Sage Emperor, your Majesty's grandfather, quelled disorder and restored order, establishing the foundations and setting the ultimate standard, grasping the essence of perfect governance and instituting simple and essential methods.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, the Civil and Martial Sage Emperor, Your Majesty's grandfather, quelled disorder and restored order, established foundations and set the supreme standard, grasped the essence of perfect governance, and instituted simple and essential methods.

sentences.zh: 省其官，清其吏，舉天下職司無一虛授，用天下財帛無一枉費。

translations.literal: He reduced the number of officials, purified the bureaucracy, ensuring that not a single official post in the empire was granted idly and not a single coin of the empire's wealth was wasted.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced officials, purified the bureaucracy, ensured not a single post in the empire was granted idly, and not a single coin of the realm's wealth was wasted.

sentences.zh: 賞必俟功，官必得俊，所為無不成，所征無不伏。

translations.literal: Rewards were bestowed only upon merit; official positions were given only to the worthy. Nothing he undertook failed to succeed; no one he campaigned against failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards awaited merit; offices went only to the worthy. Nothing he undertook failed; no one he campaigned against failed to submit.

sentences.zh: 不多造寺觀而福德自至，不多度僧尼而殃咎自滅。

translations.literal: He did not build many temples and monasteries, yet blessings and virtue came of their own accord; he did not ordain many monks and nuns, yet calamities and misfortunes vanished by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He did not build many temples and monasteries, yet blessings came of themselves; he did not ordain many monks and nuns, yet calamities vanished of themselves.

sentences.zh: 道合乎天地，德通乎神明。

translations.literal: His Way harmonized with Heaven and Earth; his virtue communicated with the divine spirits.
translations.idiomatic: His Way harmonized with Heaven and Earth; his virtue reached the divine spirits.

sentences.zh: 故天地憐之，神明祐之，使陰陽不愆，風雨合度。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven and Earth cherished him and the divine spirits protected him, causing yin and yang to be without fault and wind and rain to be timely.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Heaven and Earth cherished him and the divine spirits protected him, so yin and yang were without fault and wind and rain were timely.

sentences.zh: 四人樂其業，五谷遂其成，腐粟爛帛，填街委巷。

translations.literal: The four classes of people delighted in their occupations; the five grains achieved their full growth; surplus grain and silk rotted, filling the streets and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: The four classes delighted in their occupations; the five grains reached full harvest; surplus grain and silk rotted, filling streets and alleys.

sentences.zh: 千里萬里，貢賦於郊；

translations.literal: From a thousand li, from ten thousand li, tribute flowed to the suburbs of the capital;
translations.idiomatic: From a thousand li, from ten thousand li, tribute flowed to the capital suburbs;

sentences.zh: 九夷百蠻，歸款於闕。

translations.literal: The nine Yi and hundred Man tribes submitted their allegiance at the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: The nine Yi and hundred Man tribes submitted allegiance at the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 自有帝皇已來，未有若斯之神聖者也，故得享國久長，多歷年所，陛下何不取而則之？

translations.literal: Since the beginning of emperors and kings, there has never been one as divine and sagely as this; thus he was able to enjoy a long reign spanning many years. Why does your Majesty not take him as your model?
translations.idiomatic: Since emperors and kings began, none has been so divine and sagely; thus he enjoyed a long reign over many years. Why does Your Majesty not take him as a model?

sentences.zh: 中宗孝和皇帝，陛下之兄，居先人之業，忽先人之化，不取賢良之言，而恣子女之意。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong, the Filial and Harmonious Emperor, your Majesty's elder brother, inheriting the enterprise of his ancestors, neglected their transformative teachings; he did not heed the words of the worthy and good but indulged the whims of his children.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong, the Filial and Harmonious Emperor, Your Majesty's elder brother, inherited his ancestors' enterprise but neglected their transformative teachings; he did not heed worthy counsel but indulged his children's whims.

sentences.zh: 官爵非擇，虛食祿者數千人；

translations.literal: Official ranks and titles were not chosen with care; several thousand idly consumed salaries;
translations.idiomatic: Official ranks were not chosen with care; several thousand idly consumed salaries;

sentences.zh: 封建無功，妄食土者百餘戶。

translations.literal: Fiefs were granted without merit; over a hundred households improperly held land.
translations.idiomatic: Fiefs were granted without merit; over a hundred households improperly held land.

sentences.zh: 造寺不止，枉費財者數百億；

translations.literal: He ceaselessly built temples, wasting wealth amounting to tens of billions;
translations.idiomatic: He ceaselessly built temples, wasting wealth amounting to tens of billions;

sentences.zh: 度人不休，免租庸者數十萬。

translations.literal: He endlessly ordained people, exempting hundreds of thousands from taxes and corvee.
translations.idiomatic: He endlessly ordained people, exempting hundreds of thousands from taxes and corvee.

sentences.zh: 是使國家所出加數倍，所入減數倍。

translations.literal: This caused the state's expenditures to increase severalfold while its income decreased severalfold.
translations.idiomatic: This caused state expenditures to increase severalfold while income decreased severalfold.

sentences.zh: 倉不停卒歲之儲，庫不貯一時之帛。

translations.literal: The granaries held no store sufficient for a year; the treasuries held no silk sufficient for a season.
translations.idiomatic: The granaries held no store for a year's end; the treasuries held no silk for a season.

sentences.zh: 所惡者逐，逐多忠良；

translations.literal: Those he disliked were banished, and among the banished were many loyal and good;
translations.idiomatic: Those he disliked were banished, and many of the banished were loyal and good;

sentences.zh: 所愛者賞，賞多讒慝。

translations.literal: Those he loved were rewarded, and among the rewarded were many slanderers and evil-doers.
translations.idiomatic: Those he loved were rewarded, and many of the rewarded were slanderers and villains.

sentences.zh: 朋佞喋喋，交相傾動。

translations.literal: Cliques of flatterers chattered incessantly, vying to topple each other.
translations.idiomatic: Cliques of flatterers chattered incessantly, vying to topple one another.

sentences.zh: 容身不為於朝廷，保位皆由於黨附。

translations.literal: Maintaining one's position at court was not through personal integrity but through attachment to factions.
translations.idiomatic: Maintaining one's position at court came not through personal integrity but through factional attachment.

sentences.zh: 奪百姓之食，以養殘兇；

translations.literal: He seized the food of the common people to nourish the cruel and vicious;
translations.idiomatic: He seized the people's food to nourish the cruel and vicious;

sentences.zh: 剝萬人之衣，以塗土木。

translations.literal: He stripped the clothing from ten thousand to adorn buildings of wood and earth.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped clothing from ten thousand to adorn buildings of wood and earth.

sentences.zh: 於是人怨神怒，親忿眾離，水旱不調，疾疫屢起。

translations.literal: Consequently men resented and spirits raged, kin were angered and the multitude alienated; floods and droughts were unseasonable, epidemics and plagues arose repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Consequently men resented and spirits raged, kin were angered and the multitude alienated; floods and droughts were unseasonable and epidemics arose repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 遠近殊論，公私罄然。

translations.literal: Near and far opinions differed; public and private resources were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far opinions differed; public and private resources were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 五六年間，再三禍變，享國不永，受終於兇婦人。

translations.literal: Within five or six years calamities and upheavals occurred again and again; he did not enjoy a long reign and his rule ended with a vicious woman.
translations.idiomatic: Within five or six years calamities recurred; he did not enjoy a long reign and met his end at the hands of a vicious woman.

sentences.zh: 寺舍不能保其身，僧尼不能護妻子，取譏萬代，見笑四夷。

translations.literal: The temple buildings could not protect his person; the monks and nuns could not protect his wife and children. He earned the ridicule of ten thousand generations and the laughter of the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Temples could not protect his person; monks and nuns could not protect his wife and children. He earned ridicule for ten thousand generations and laughter from the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 此陛下之所眼見也，何不除而改之。

translations.literal: This your Majesty has seen with your own eyes. Why not eradicate and reform it?
translations.idiomatic: This Your Majesty has seen with your own eyes. Why not eradicate and reform it?

sentences.zh: 依太宗之理國，則百官以理，百姓無憂，故太山之安立可致矣；

translations.literal: If we follow Taizong's way of governing the state, then the hundred officials will be well-ordered and the common people will have no worries; thus the security of Mount Tai can readily be achieved;
translations.idiomatic: If Taizong's way of governing is followed, the hundred officials will be well-ordered and the people will have no worries; thus the security of Mount Tai can readily be achieved;

sentences.zh: 依中宗之理國，則萬人以怨，百事不寧，故累卵之危立可致矣。

translations.literal: If we follow Zhongzong's way of governing the state, then ten thousand people will harbor resentment and a hundred affairs will not be tranquil; thus the peril of piled eggs can readily be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhongzong's way of governing is followed, ten thousand people will harbor resentment and a hundred affairs will be unsettled; thus the peril of piled eggs can readily be achieved.

sentences.zh: 頃自夏已來，霪雨不解，谷荒於壟，麥爛於場。

translations.literal: Recently since summer continuous rain has not ceased; grain lies wasted in the fields and wheat rots on the threshing grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Recently since summer continuous rain has not ceased; grain lies wasted in the fields and wheat rots on the threshing grounds.

sentences.zh: 入秋已來，亢旱成災，苗而不實，霜損蟲暴，草葉枯黃。

translations.literal: Since entering autumn severe drought has caused disaster; seedlings do not bear fruit, frost damages and insects ravage, grass and leaves wither and yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Since autumn began severe drought has brought disaster; seedlings fail to bear fruit, frost and insects ravage, and grass and leaves wither yellow.

sentences.zh: 下人咨嗟，未知赒賑；

translations.literal: The lower people lament, yet relief is unknown;
translations.idiomatic: The common people lament, yet relief is unknown;

sentences.zh: 而營寺造觀，日繼於時，檢校試官，充臺溢署。

translations.literal: Yet the construction of temples and monasteries continues daily without pause, and the offices of inspectors and probationary officials overflow the ministries and bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Yet temple and monastery construction continues daily without pause, and inspector and probationary offices overflow the ministries and bureaus.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下愛兩女，為造兩觀，燒瓦運木，載土填坑，道路流言，皆云計用錢百餘萬貫。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that your Majesty, loving your two daughters, builds two monasteries for them, burning tiles, transporting timber, carrying earth to fill pits. Rumors in the streets all say the planned cost exceeds a million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, loving your two daughters, is building two monasteries for them, burning tiles, transporting timber, carrying earth to fill pits. Street rumors all say the planned cost exceeds a million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下，聖人也，無所不知；

translations.literal: Your Majesty is a sage; there is nothing you do not know;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is a sage; there is nothing you do not know;

sentences.zh: 陛下，明君也，無所不見。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is an enlightened ruler; there is nothing you do not see.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is an enlightened ruler; there is nothing you do not see.

sentences.zh: 既知且見，知倉有幾年之儲，庫有幾年之帛？

translations.literal: Since you know and see, do you know how many years' store the granaries hold? How many years' silk the treasuries hold?
translations.idiomatic: Since you know and see, do you know how many years' stores the granaries hold? How many years' silk the treasuries hold?

sentences.zh: 知百姓之間可存活乎？

translations.literal: Do you know whether the common people can survive?
translations.idiomatic: Do you know whether the common people can survive?

sentences.zh: 三邊之上可轉輸乎？

translations.literal: Whether supplies can be transported to the three frontiers?
translations.idiomatic: Whether supplies can be transported to the three frontiers?

sentences.zh: 當今發一卒以禦邊陲，遣一兵以衛社稷，多無衣食，皆帶饑寒。

translations.literal: At present when we dispatch a single soldier to defend the border regions or send a single soldier to guard the altars of state, most have no clothing or food and all bear hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: At present when a single soldier is dispatched to defend the frontiers or guard the altars of state, most lack clothing and food and all bear hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 賞賜之間，迥無所出，軍旅驟敗，莫不由斯。

translations.literal: When it comes to rewards and gifts there is absolutely nothing to give; armies are suddenly defeated, none not due to this.
translations.idiomatic: When it comes to rewards and gifts there is nothing to give; armies are suddenly defeated, all for this reason.

sentences.zh: 而乃以百萬貫錢造無用之觀，以受六合之怨乎！

translations.literal: And yet you would use a million strings of cash to build useless monasteries, thereby incurring the resentment of all within the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: And yet a million strings of cash are spent to build useless monasteries, incurring the resentment of all within the four seas!

sentences.zh: 以違萬人之心乎！

translations.literal: Thereby opposing the hearts of ten thousand people!
translations.idiomatic: Thereby opposing the hearts of ten thousand people!

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下續阿韋之醜跡，而不改阿韋之亂政。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that your Majesty continues the ugly traces of Lady Wei yet does not reform Lady Wei's chaotic governance.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty continues the ugly traces of Lady Wei yet does not reform Lady Wei's chaotic governance.

sentences.zh: 忍棄太宗之理本，不忍棄中宗之亂階；

translations.literal: You can bear to discard Taizong's fundamental principles of order but cannot bear to discard Zhongzong's steps to chaos;
translations.idiomatic: You can bear to discard Taizong's fundamental principles of order but cannot bear to discard Zhongzong's steps to chaos;

sentences.zh: 忍棄太宗久長之謀，不忍棄中宗短促之計。

translations.literal: You can bear to discard Taizong's long-term plans but cannot bear to discard Zhongzong's short-sighted schemes.
translations.idiomatic: You can bear to discard Taizong's long-term plans but cannot bear to discard Zhongzong's short-sighted schemes.

sentences.zh: 陛下又何以繼祖宗、觀萬國。

translations.literal: How then will your Majesty succeed the ancestors and be observed by the myriad states?
translations.idiomatic: How then will Your Majesty succeed the ancestors and be observed by the myriad states?

sentences.zh: 昔陛下為皇太子，在阿韋之時，危亡是懼，常切齒於群兇。

translations.literal: In the past when your Majesty was Crown Prince, in the time of Lady Wei, you feared peril and ruin and constantly gnashed your teeth at the crowd of villains.
translations.idiomatic: In the past when Your Majesty was Crown Prince, in Lady Wei's time, you feared peril and ruin and constantly gnashed your teeth at the crowd of villains.

sentences.zh: 今貴為天子，富有海內，而不改群兇之事，臣恐復有切齒於陛下者也，陛下又何以非群兇而誅之？

translations.literal: Now honored as the Son of Heaven, possessing the wealth of the land within the seas, if you do not reform the affairs of that crowd of villains, I fear there will again be those who gnash their teeth at your Majesty. How then can your Majesty condemn that crowd of villains and execute them?
translations.idiomatic: Now honored as Son of Heaven, possessing wealth within the seas, if you do not reform the affairs of that crowd of villains, I fear there will again be those who gnash their teeth at Your Majesty. How then can Your Majesty condemn those villains and execute them?

sentences.zh: 臣往見明敕，自今已後，一依貞觀故事。

translations.literal: I previously saw a clear imperial decree stating that henceforth everything should follow the precedents of the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: I previously saw a clear edict stating that henceforth everything should follow Zhenguan precedents.

sentences.zh: 且貞觀之時，豈有今日之造寺營觀，加僧尼道士，益無用之官，行不急之務，而亂政者也！

translations.literal: Moreover in the Zhenguan era was there such building of temples and monasteries as today, such increase of monks, nuns, and Daoist priests, such multiplication of useless officials, such pursuit of non-urgent tasks, thus creating chaotic governance!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover in the Zhenguan era was there such building of temples and monasteries, such increase of monks, nuns, and Daoist priests, such multiplication of useless officials, and such pursuit of non-urgent tasks leading to chaotic governance!

sentences.zh: 臣以為棄其言而不行其信，慕其善而不遷其惡，陛下又何以刑於四海？

translations.literal: I believe that to discard their words and not keep faith with them, to admire their goodness and not change their evils—how then will your Majesty set an example for all within the four seas?
translations.idiomatic: I believe that to discard their words and not keep faith, to admire their goodness and not change their evils—how then will Your Majesty set an example for all within the four seas?

sentences.zh: 往者，和帝之憐悖逆也，為奸人之所誤，宗晉卿勸為第宅，趙履溫勸為園亭，損數百家之居，侵數百家之地。

translations.literal: In the past Emperor He's pity for the rebellious was misled by treacherous men. Zong Jinqing urged the building of mansions; Zhao Luwen urged the building of gardens and pavilions, destroying the dwellings of several hundred families and encroaching on the land of several hundred families.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Emperor He's pity for the rebellious was misled by treacherous men. Zong Jinqing urged building mansions; Zhao Luwen urged building gardens and pavilions, destroying the dwellings of several hundred families and encroaching on the land of several hundred families.

sentences.zh: 工徒斫而未息，義兵紛以交馳，卒使亭不得遊，宅不得坐。

translations.literal: Craftsmen and laborers hewed without rest; righteous troops rushed about in confusion, finally making it so the pavilions could not be enjoyed and the mansions could not be dwelt in.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen and laborers hewed without rest; righteous troops rushed about in confusion, until the pavilions could not be enjoyed and the mansions could not be occupied.

sentences.zh: 信邪佞之說，成骨肉之刑，此陛下之所眼見也。

translations.literal: Believing the words of evil flatterers, he brought about punishment upon his own flesh and blood. This your Majesty has seen with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Believing evil flatterers, he brought punishment upon his own flesh and blood. This Your Majesty has seen with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 今茲造觀，臣必知非陛下、公主之本意，得無趙履溫之徒將勸為之，冀誤其骨肉，不可不明察也。

translations.literal: Now building these monasteries, I certainly know it is not the original intention of your Majesty and the Princesses. Might it not be that men like Zhao Luwen are urging it, hoping to mislead your flesh and blood? This cannot but be clearly examined.
translations.idiomatic: Now in building these monasteries, I know it is not the original intention of Your Majesty and the princesses. Might men like Zhao Luwen be urging it, hoping to mislead your flesh and blood? This must be clearly examined.

sentences.zh: 臣聞出家修道者，不預人事，專清其身心，以虛泊為高，以無為為妙，依兩卷《老子》，視一軀天尊，無欲無營，不損不害。

translations.literal: I have heard that those who leave their families to cultivate the Way do not involve themselves in human affairs but purely purify their bodies and minds, considering emptiness and detachment as lofty and non-action as wondrous, relying on the two scrolls of the Laozi, contemplating the single form of the Heavenly Venerable, having no desires and no striving, not harming and not injuring.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who leave home to cultivate the Way do not involve themselves in human affairs but purify body and mind, taking emptiness and detachment as lofty and non-action as wondrous, relying on the two scrolls of the Laozi, contemplating the Heavenly Venerable, without desire or striving, without harm or injury.

sentences.zh: 何必璇臺玉榭，寶像珍龕，使人困窮，然後為道哉！

translations.literal: Why must there be jade terraces and jeweled pavilions, precious images and rare shrines, reducing people to poverty and distress, and only then consider it the Way!
translations.idiomatic: Why must there be jade terraces and jeweled pavilions, precious images and rare shrines, reducing people to poverty and distress, and only then call it the Way!

sentences.zh: 且舊觀足可歸依，無造無營，以取窮竭。

translations.literal: Moreover the old monasteries are sufficient for reliance; do not build, do not strive, thereby causing exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the old monasteries are sufficient for devotion; do not build, do not strive, thereby causing exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 若此行之三年，國不富，人不安，朝廷不清，陛下不樂，則臣請殺身於朝，以令天下言事者。

translations.literal: If after practicing this for three years the state is not wealthy, the people are not secure, the court is not pure, and your Majesty is not happy, then I beg to be executed at court to serve as a warning to all under heaven who speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If after this course is followed for three years the state is not wealthy, the people are not secure, the court is not pure, and Your Majesty is not happy, then I beg to be executed at court as a warning to all who speak on affairs under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下行非常之惠，權停兩觀，以俟豐年。

translations.literal: I humbly beg your Majesty to exercise extraordinary grace, temporarily halting the two monasteries until a year of plenty.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to exercise extraordinary grace, temporarily halting the two monasteries until a year of plenty.

sentences.zh: 以兩觀之財，為公主施貧窮，填府庫，則公主福德無窮矣。

translations.literal: Use the wealth for the two monasteries to allow the Princesses to bestow alms on the poor and fill the government treasuries; then the Princesses' blessings and virtue will be boundless.
translations.idiomatic: Use the wealth for the two monasteries to allow the princesses to give alms to the poor and fill the treasuries; then the princesses' blessings and virtue will be boundless.

sentences.zh: 不然，臣恐下人怨望，不減於前朝之時。

translations.literal: If not, I fear the resentment of the lower people will be no less than in the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: If not, I fear popular resentment will be no less than in the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 前朝之時，賢愚知敗，人雖有口而不敢言，言未發聲，禍將及矣。

translations.literal: In the previous reign the worthy and foolish knew of the ruin; though men had mouths they dared not speak. Before the sound of speech was uttered calamity was about to strike.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous reign the worthy and foolish knew ruin was coming; though men had mouths they dared not speak. Before words were uttered calamity was about to strike.

sentences.zh: 韋月將受誅於丹僥，燕欽融見殺於紫庭，此人皆不惜其身而納忠於主，身既死矣，朝亦危矣。

translations.literal: Wei Yuejiang was executed at Dandiao; Yan Qinrong was killed in the Purple Court. These men all did not cherish their own persons but offered loyalty to their lord. Their persons dead, the court was also endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuejiang was executed at Dandiao; Yan Qinrong was killed in the Purple Court. These men did not cherish their own lives but offered loyalty to their lord. With their lives gone, the court was also endangered.

sentences.zh: 故先朝誅之，陛下賞之，是陛下知直言之士有裨於國。

translations.literal: Therefore the previous reign executed them but your Majesty rewards them. This shows your Majesty knows that outspoken scholars benefit the state.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the previous reign executed them but Your Majesty rewards them. This shows Your Majesty knows that outspoken scholars benefit the state.

sentences.zh: 臣今直言，亦先代之直，惟陛下察之。

translations.literal: My outspoken words now are also the outspokenness of former generations. I beg your Majesty to consider this.
translations.idiomatic: My outspoken words now are also the outspokenness of former generations. I beg Your Majesty to consider this.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，睿宗嘉其公直。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Ruizong commended his fairness and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong praised his fairness and uprightness when the memorial was submitted.

sentences.zh: 稍遷為右臺殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Palace Censor of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Palace Censor of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 開元中，累轉潁王府長史。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan he was repeatedly transferred to chief administrator of the Prince of Ying's household.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan he rose to chief administrator of the Prince of Ying's household.

sentences.zh: 天寶初卒，年八十余。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he died at age over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in Tianbao at over eighty.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫好聞其善，惡聞其過，君人者之常情也；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: To love hearing of one's goodness and hate hearing of one's faults is the common disposition of rulers;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: To love hearing praise and hate hearing fault is the common disposition of rulers;

sentences.zh: 寧諂媚以取容，不逆耳以招禍，臣人者之常情也。

translations.literal: to prefer flattery to win favor rather than unwelcome words that invite disaster is the common disposition of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: to prefer flattery for favor rather than unwelcome words that invite disaster is the common disposition of ministers.

sentences.zh: 能反此者，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: To be able to reverse this—is it not excellent!
translations.idiomatic: To reverse this—is that not excellence itself?

sentences.zh: 李、薛等六君，吐忠讜之言，補朝廷之失，有犯無隱，不愧古人，有唐之良臣也。

translations.literal: The six gentlemen Li, Xue, and the others spoke loyal and forthright words, repaired the court's failings, offended without concealment, and did not disgrace the ancients—they were worthy ministers of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Li, Xue, and the other six spoke loyal and forthright words, repaired the court's failings, and offended without concealment. They did not disgrace the ancients—they were worthy ministers of Tang.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：臣之事君，有邪有正。

translations.literal: Commentary: Commentary: In how ministers serve their ruler, there is the crooked and the straight.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In how ministers serve their ruler, there is the crooked and the straight.

sentences.zh: 君之使臣，從諫則聖。

translations.literal: In how rulers employ ministers, to follow remonstrance is sagely.
translations.idiomatic: In how rulers employ ministers, to heed remonstrance is sagely.

sentences.zh: 李、薛輸忠，救人之命。

translations.literal: Li and Xue offered loyalty and saved men's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Xue offered loyalty and saved lives.

sentences.zh: 韋、韓讜言，醫國之病。

translations.literal: Wei and Han spoke bluntly and cured the state's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Han spoke bluntly and cured the state's ills.

sentences.zh: 辛、王章疏，犯顏竦聽。

translations.literal: Xin and Wang submitted forthright memorials that offended the countenance and made the ruler listen in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Wang submitted forthright memorials that made the ruler listen in awe.

sentences.zh: 張子法言，實裨時政。

translations.literal: Zhang's words accorded with law and truly benefited current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's words accorded with law and truly benefited governance.
